```rust
/// Builds from a [`TupleView`] (`from_view*`): the rows the view matches, in
/// output-column order, become the trie's buffer at their exact size, and the
/// trie is the one a batch of those rows builds. Every case is worked out by
/// hand from the source rows (`reference`), never through
/// `TupleView::materialize`, so a bug in the view cannot hide in the oracle.
#[cfg(test)]
mod view_tests {
    use {
        super::{
            super::{
                expansion::LazyExpansion,
                identity::{assert_same_trie, configs, inputs, rows},
                pruning::SingletonPruning,
            },
            tests::walked_sorted,
            *,
        },
        crate::{cardinality::Cardinality, test_support::Mod10HashStrategy},
        kermit_iters::{Filter, FxHashStrategy},
    };

    /// Eight rows of three columns, for the hand-worked cases. Rows 0 and 4
    /// are equal, so a projection can repeat a row.
    fn hand_source() -> Tuples {
        rows(3, &[
            [1, 2, 3],
            [1, 2, 7],
            [4, 5, 6],
            [1, 9, 3],
            [1, 2, 3],
            [8, 8, 8],
            [3, 1, 1],
            [5, 3, 3],
        ])
    }

    /// A view of a three-column source, described twice: as the `Filter` and
    /// the output columns a `TupleView` takes, and as the predicate the
    /// reference build keeps rows by.
    struct Case {
        name: &'static str,
        filter: Filter,
        columns: Vec<usize>,
        keeps: fn(&[usize]) -> bool,
    }

    fn cases() -> Vec<Case> {
        vec![
            Case {
                name: "all rows, all columns",
                filter: Filter::none(),
                columns: vec![0, 1, 2],
                keeps: |_| true,
            },
            Case {
                name: "col2 = 3, columns [1, 0]",
                filter: Filter::new(vec![(2, 3)], vec![]),
                columns: vec![1, 0],
                keeps: |row| row[2] == 3,
            },
            Case {
                name: "col1 = col2, column [2]",
                filter: Filter::new(vec![], vec![(1, 2)]),
                columns: vec![2],
                keeps: |row| row[1] == row[2],
            },
            Case {
                name: "col0 = 1, columns [2, 1]",
                filter: Filter::new(vec![(0, 1)], vec![]),
                columns: vec![2, 1],
                keeps: |row| row[0] == 1,
            },
            Case {
                name: "col0 = 99 (no row), all columns",
                filter: Filter::new(vec![(0, 99)], vec![]),
                columns: vec![0, 1, 2],
                keeps: |row| row[0] == 99,
            },
        ]
    }

    /// What `case` selects from `source`, built by hand: the rows its
    /// predicate keeps, in source order, cut to its columns, in a buffer of
    /// exactly their size.
    fn reference(source: &Tuples, case: &Case) -> Tuples {
        let kept: Vec<Vec<usize>> = source
            .rows()
            .filter(|&row| (case.keeps)(row))
            .map(|row| case.columns.iter().map(|&column| row[column]).collect())
            .collect();
        let mut batch = Tuples::with_capacity(case.columns.len(), kept.len());
        for row in &kept {
            batch.push(row);
        }
        batch
    }

    /// The shared three-column inputs, and the hand-worked source.
    fn sources() -> Vec<(&'static str, Tuples)> {
        let mut sources = inputs(3);
        sources.push(("hand", hand_source()));
        sources
    }

    /// The fixture is not vacuous: the hand source keeps 8, 4, 3 and 4 rows
    /// under the first four cases, and none under the last.
    #[test]
    fn the_hand_source_exercises_every_case() {
        let source = hand_source();
        let kept: Vec<usize> = cases()
            .iter()
            .map(|case| reference(&source, case).len())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(kept, vec![8, 4, 3, 4, 0]);
    }

    /// A trie built from `case`'s view of each source is the trie its
    /// hand-made batch builds, array for array (the buffer at its exact
    /// capacity, the links, every table, chain, singleton and pending chain),
    /// under every config, for the layout `H`, `P`, `E`.
    fn check_views_build_their_batches<H: HashStrategy, P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>() {
        for (input, source) in sources() {
            for case in cases() {
                let arity = case.columns.len();
                let expected = reference(&source, &case);
                for config in configs() {
                    let label = format!(
                        "{}/{}/{} {input}, {}, load {}%, root {}, children {}",
                        H::NAME,
                        P::NAME,
                        E::NAME,
                        case.name,
                        config.load_factor.numerator(),
                        config.root_capacity.axis_value(),
                        config.child_capacity.axis_value(),
                    );
                    let view = TupleView::new(&source, case.filter.clone(), case.columns.clone());
                    let built =
                        HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_view_with_config(arity.into(), config, view);
                    let batch = HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_tuples_with_config(
                        arity.into(),
                        config,
                        expected.clone(),
                    );
                    assert_same_trie(&batch, &built, &label);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_view_builds_the_trie_its_batch_builds() {
        check_views_build_their_batches::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>();
        check_views_build_their_batches::<FxHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, EagerExpansion>();
        check_views_build_their_batches::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, LazyExpansion>();
        check_views_build_their_batches::<Mod10HashStrategy, SingletonPruning, LazyExpansion>();
    }

    /// The buffer is the view's matching rows, in source order and in output
    /// column order, in exactly their size however much spare capacity the
    /// source has: worked out here by hand. `col2 = 3` keeps rows 0, 3, 4 and
    /// 7 of the hand source, read as columns `[1, 0]`.
    #[test]
    fn the_buffer_is_the_views_rows_at_their_exact_size() {
        let mut source = Tuples::with_capacity(3, 100);
        for row in hand_source().rows() {
            source.push(row);
        }
        assert!(
            source.value_capacity() > 3 * 8,
            "the premise: the source has spare capacity"
        );
        let view = TupleView::new(&source, Filter::new(vec![(2, 3)], vec![]), vec![1, 0]);
        let trie: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view(2.into(), view);
        assert_eq!(trie.collect_tuples().to_vecs(), vec![
            vec![2, 1],
            vec![9, 1],
            vec![2, 1],
            vec![3, 5]
        ]);
        assert_eq!(
            trie.tuples().value_capacity(),
            4 * 2,
            "exactly the four rows"
        );
        assert_eq!(trie.links().len(), 4, "one link per matching row");
        assert_eq!(trie.tuple_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(walked_sorted(&trie), vec![
            vec![2, 1],
            vec![2, 1],
            vec![3, 5],
            vec![9, 1]
        ]);
    }

    /// `root-capacity=tuples` sizes the root by the rows the view matches,
    /// not by the rows of its source: 34 of the 100 rows have `col1 = 0`.
    #[test]
    fn the_root_is_sized_by_the_matching_rows() {
        let config = HashTrieConfig {
            root_capacity: RootCapacity::Tuples,
            ..HashTrieConfig::default()
        };
        let mut source = Tuples::with_capacity(2, 100);
        for k in 0..100 {
            source.push(&[k, k % 3]);
        }
        let view = TupleView::new(&source, Filter::new(vec![(1, 0)], vec![]), vec![0]);
        assert_eq!(view.count(), 34, "the premise");
        assert_ne!(
            config.root_log2_capacity(34),
            config.root_log2_capacity(100),
            "the premise: 34 rows and 100 rows need different roots"
        );
        let trie: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_config(1.into(), config, view);
        assert_eq!(
            trie.root().buckets_len().trailing_zeros(),
            config.root_log2_capacity(34)
        );
        assert_eq!(trie.tuple_count(), 34);
    }

    /// An empty source builds an empty trie under any header, as
    /// `from_tuples(header, vec![])` does, whatever arity the view claims: it
    /// holds no row to disagree with the header. A later `insert` then pushes
    /// into a buffer of the header's arity.
    #[test]
    fn an_empty_source_builds_an_empty_trie_under_any_header() {
        let source = Tuples::new(0);
        let mut trie: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view(2.into(), TupleView::all(&source));
        assert_eq!(trie.header().arity(), 2);
        assert_eq!(trie.tuples().arity(), 2);
        assert_eq!(trie.tuple_count(), 0);
        trie.insert(vec![1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(walked_sorted(&trie), vec![vec![1, 2]]);
    }

    /// Dropping a column can make two rows equal. `HashTrie` is a multiset,
    /// so the trie keeps both.
    #[test]
    fn a_projection_that_repeats_a_row_keeps_both() {
        let source = rows(3, &[[1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 4], [5, 6, 7]]);
        let view = TupleView::new(&source, Filter::none(), vec![0, 1]);
        let trie: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view(2.into(), view);
        assert_eq!(trie.tuple_count(), 3);
        assert_eq!(walked_sorted(&trie), vec![
            vec![1, 2],
            vec![1, 2],
            vec![5, 6]
        ]);
    }

    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "from_tuples: tuple arity 1 does not match header arity 2")]
    fn a_view_of_the_wrong_arity_panics() {
        let source = hand_source();
        let view = TupleView::new(&source, Filter::none(), vec![0]);
        let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view(2.into(), view);
    }

    /// The check does not wait for a row to pass the filter: it fires
    /// whenever the source holds rows (Amendment 1, item 6). Here the filter
    /// rejects all eight.
    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "from_tuples: tuple arity 1 does not match header arity 2")]
    fn a_filter_that_rejects_every_row_does_not_excuse_the_arity() {
        let source = hand_source();
        let view = TupleView::new(&source, Filter::new(vec![(0, 99)], vec![]), vec![0]);
        let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view(2.into(), view);
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// Creates a trie holding `config`, populated with the rows `view`
    /// selects and built by `mode`: the view-reading form of
    /// [`from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode`](Self::from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode),
    /// and the constructor every `from_view*` ends in. The matching rows are
    /// copied once, in output-column order, into a buffer of exactly their
    /// size (`TupleView::materialize`), and every mode builds over that
    /// buffer: `bulk` and `incremental` keep it as the trie's own, and the
    /// partitioning modes still copy it again into partition order, until
    /// their builds read the view themselves. The root is sized by the
    /// number of matching rows, never by the source's.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if the view's source holds rows and the view's arity is not
    /// `header.arity()`, whether or not any row passes the view's filter,
    /// and where `from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode` panics for a mode
    /// whose prerequisite `config` lacks.
    pub fn from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
        header: RelationHeader, config: HashTrieConfig, mode: HashTrieBuildMode,
        view: TupleView<'_>,
    ) -> Self {
        let batch = Self::batch_from_view(&header, &view);
        Self::from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode(header, config, mode, batch)
    }

    /// The batch a trie for `header` stores for `view`, after the arity check
    /// every build from a view makes first: its matching rows, copied once
    /// into a buffer of exactly their size (`TupleView::materialize`), or,
    /// when the source is empty, an empty batch of the header's arity, since
    /// an empty source carries no arity worth keeping and `insert` must later
    /// push rows of the header's.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics as `relation::check_view_arity` does, the one check of every
    /// structure: if `view.source_rows() > 0` and the view's arity is not
    /// `header.arity()`, with the message the per-tuple check gave before
    /// #111. A filter that rejects every row is no excuse: the check looks at
    /// the source, not at the rows that pass.
    fn batch_from_view(header: &RelationHeader, view: &TupleView<'_>) -> Tuples {
        crate::relation::check_view_arity(header, view);
        if view.source_rows() == 0 {
            return Tuples::new(header.arity());
        }
        view.materialize()
    }
```

```rust
    /// `incremental` over a view builds the trie `bulk` builds from the
    /// view's hand-made batch, array for array, links included (the two
    /// builds are array-identical), under every config that accepts it:
    /// children that grow.
    fn check_incremental_views_build_the_bulk_trie<
        H: HashStrategy,
        P: PruningPolicy,
        E: ExpansionPolicy,
    >() {
        for (input, source) in sources() {
            for case in cases() {
                let arity = case.columns.len();
                let expected = reference(&source, &case);
                for config in incremental_configs() {
                    let label = format!(
                        "{}/{}/{} {input}, {}, load {}%, root {}",
                        H::NAME,
                        P::NAME,
                        E::NAME,
                        case.name,
                        config.load_factor.numerator(),
                        config.root_capacity.axis_value(),
                    );
                    let view = TupleView::new(&source, case.filter.clone(), case.columns.clone());
                    let built = HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
                        arity.into(),
                        config,
                        HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental,
                        view,
                    );
                    let bulk = HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_tuples_with_config(
                        arity.into(),
                        config,
                        expected.clone(),
                    );
                    assert_same_trie(&bulk, &built, &label);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn incremental_over_a_view_builds_the_bulk_trie() {
        check_incremental_views_build_the_bulk_trie::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>();
        check_incremental_views_build_the_bulk_trie::<
            FxHashStrategy,
            SingletonPruning,
            EagerExpansion,
        >();
        check_incremental_views_build_the_bulk_trie::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, LazyExpansion>();
        check_incremental_views_build_the_bulk_trie::<
            Mod10HashStrategy,
            SingletonPruning,
            LazyExpansion,
        >();
    }

    /// `bulk` and `incremental` build the same trie, so only
    /// `BULK_BUILDS` tells which ran: `from_view`, `from_view_with_config`
    /// and `Bulk` take Algorithm 2, `Incremental` the per-tuple build.
    #[test]
    fn each_build_mode_runs_its_own_build_from_a_view() {
        let source = hand_source();
        let view = || TupleView::all(&source);
        let bulk_builds = |build: &dyn Fn()| {
            BULK_BUILDS.with(|n| n.set(0));
            build();
            BULK_BUILDS.with(std::cell::Cell::get)
        };
        assert_eq!(
            bulk_builds(&|| {
                let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view(3.into(), view());
            }),
            1,
            "from_view"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            bulk_builds(&|| {
                let _: HashTrie =
                    HashTrie::from_view_with_config(3.into(), HashTrieConfig::default(), view());
            }),
            1,
            "from_view_with_config"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            bulk_builds(&|| {
                let _: HashTrie =
                    HashTrie::from_view_with_build_mode(3.into(), HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk, view());
            }),
            1,
            "bulk"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            bulk_builds(&|| {
                let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_build_mode(
                    3.into(),
                    HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental,
                    view(),
                );
            }),
            0,
            "incremental"
        );
    }

    /// `insert_at` creates a child on its first tuple, before the child's
    /// list is known, so `incremental` cannot size it: the prerequisite
    /// holds from a view too.
    #[test]

    fn incremental_over_a_view_requires_grown_children() {

        let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(

    /// `presized:N` cuts its regions from a root sized before any tuple
    /// arrives, so it requires `root-capacity=tuples` from a view too.
    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "hash-trie=presized:2 requires root-capacity=tuples")]
    fn presized_over_a_view_requires_a_presized_root() {
        let source = hand_source();
        let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
            3.into(),
            HashTrieConfig::default(),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Presized(Threads::new(2).expect("two is a valid thread count")),

    /// The partitioning builds of a view are the partitioning builds of the
    /// batch the view selects: the same trie, buffer and ids included, since
    /// both copy the same rows into the same partition order.
    #[test]
    fn partitioning_builds_of_a_view_match_those_of_its_batch() {
        let threads = Threads::new(2).expect("two is a valid thread count");
        let modes = [
            HashTrieBuildMode::Radix(RadixBits::new(3).expect("three is a valid bit count")),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Parallel(threads),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Presized(threads),
        ];
        // `presized:N` requires a presized root; the others accept it.
        let config = HashTrieConfig {
            root_capacity: RootCapacity::Tuples,
            ..HashTrieConfig::default()
        };
        for (input, source) in sources() {
            for case in cases() {
                let arity = case.columns.len();
                let expected = reference(&source, &case);
                for mode in modes {
                    let label = format!("{input}, {}, {mode:?}", case.name);
                    let view = TupleView::new(&source, case.filter.clone(), case.columns.clone());
                    let built: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
                        arity.into(),
                        config,
                        mode,
                        view,
                    );
                    let batch: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode(
                        arity.into(),
                        config,
                        mode,
                        expected.clone(),
                    );
                    assert_same_trie(&batch, &built, &label);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The trait constructors agree with the inherent one, and
    /// `BuildModeRelation` builds with the default config.
    #[test]
    fn the_trait_constructors_build_from_views() {
        let source = hand_source();
        let view = || TupleView::new(&source, Filter::new(vec![(0, 1)], vec![]), vec![2, 1]);
        let radix = HashTrieBuildMode::Radix(RadixBits::new(2).expect("two is a valid bit count"));
        let config = HashTrieConfig::default();
        let inherent: HashTrie =
            HashTrie::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(2.into(), config, radix, view());
        let by_mode: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_build_mode(2.into(), radix, view());
        let by_trait: HashTrie = ConfiguredBuildModeRelation::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
            2.into(),
            config,
            radix,
            view(),
        );
        assert_same_trie(&inherent, &by_mode, "BuildModeRelation");
        assert_same_trie(&inherent, &by_trait, "ConfiguredBuildModeRelation");
        assert_eq!(*by_mode.config(), config);
    }

    /// Every constructor refuses a view of the wrong arity over a source
    /// that holds rows, even when its filter rejects every one. A
    /// constructor that quietly built the empty trie would leave a wrong
    /// header for the join to trip over.
    #[test]
    fn every_constructor_checks_the_arity_of_a_non_empty_source() {
        use std::panic::{catch_unwind, AssertUnwindSafe};
        let source = hand_source();
        // Rejects all eight rows, and reads one column into a two-column header.
        let wrong = || TupleView::new(&source, Filter::new(vec![(0, 99)], vec![]), vec![0]);
        let config = HashTrieConfig::default();
        let bulk = HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk;
        let constructors: Vec<(&str, Box<dyn Fn() + '_>)> = vec![
            ("from_view", Box::new(|| {
                let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view(2.into(), wrong());
            })),
            ("from_view_with_config", Box::new(|| {
                let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_config(2.into(), config, wrong());
            })),
            ("from_view_with_build_mode", Box::new(|| {
                let _: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_view_with_build_mode(2.into(), bulk, wrong());
            })),
            ("ConfiguredBuildModeRelation", Box::new(|| {
                let _: HashTrie = ConfiguredBuildModeRelation::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
                    2.into(),
                    config,
                    bulk,
                    wrong(),
                );
            })),
        ];
        let silent: Vec<&str> = constructors
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, build)| catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(build)).is_ok())
            .map(|(name, _)| *name)
            .collect();
        assert!(
            silent.is_empty(),
            "these constructors accept a view of the wrong arity: {silent:?}"
        );
    }
```

## Story 6: HashTrie's partitioning builds read views

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit-ds/src/morsel.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/hash_trie/radix.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/hash_trie/parallel.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/hash_trie/implementation.rs`
- **Interfaces:** uses Stories 1–3 and 5; changes `morsel::partition_rows` to take a view (Names contract: kermit-ds); exposes nothing
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit-ds --lib`
- **Review:** deep

After Story 5, `HashTrie`'s `radix:K`, `parallel:N` and `presized:N` builds still materialise a
view into a batch and then copy that batch again into partition order: two copies. This story
makes the partition copy the only one. `morsel::partition_rows` reads a `TupleView`: its
counting pass skips rows the filter rejects (`matches`), its scatter pass writes output rows
straight into the copy (`write`), `origin` holds source row ids, and the copy is sized exactly
(the old `value_capacity` inheritance is gone). `radix::fill_root`, `parallel::fill_root` and
`parallel::fill_presized_root` take `&TupleView` instead of a `Tuples` they consume, the links
are sized by `view.count()`, and the dispatch, the inherent `from_view_with_config_and_build_mode`
of Task 5.1 (the trait method of that name delegates to it, as Task 5.2 made it), calls them
directly. The inherent tuple constructor's arms for these three modes now go through that
dispatch over `TupleView::all`, so each of those modes' build exists once, in the view dispatch.
The tuple constructor keeps its `bulk` and `incremental` arms untouched, as a stopgap that
Story 7 removes by reducing it to a one-line delegation.

- **Task 6.1** changes `partition_rows` and nothing above it: its callers wrap their batch in
  `TupleView::all`. New morsel tests cover filters, equalities, projections and permutations
  across morsel boundaries. The capacity tests now expect exact sizes.
- **Task 6.2** passes the view down: the three fills, the shared `from_view_partitioned`
  (which replaces `from_tuples_partitioned`), and the dispatch.
- **Task 6.3** adds mode-equivalence tests over filtered, permuted views, and a test that a
  view matching nothing starts no worker.

The links are still written under the rules the module docs state (one writer per link), and
no code that threads them changes. The story's code holds none of the profile's landmine
markers.

```rust
    /// The copy is sized exactly: `len · arity` values, whatever spare
    /// capacity the source has, so a trie that keeps the copy holds only the
    /// bytes its rows need and `space` does not depend on how the source was
    /// built.
    #[test]
    fn partition_rows_sizes_the_copy_exactly() {
        let mut input = Tuples::with_capacity(3, 40);
        for i in 0..10 {
            input.push(&[i, i, i]);
        }
        assert!(

            assert_eq!(out.tuples.value_capacity(), 30, "threads {t}");

    /// Over `rows_of_arity(100, 3)`, the rows `[i % 7, i, 100 - i]`: this view
    /// keeps the 14 rows with `i % 7 == 3`, read as columns `[2, 1]`, so its
    /// output rows are `[100 - i, i]` and `first_mod_3` sees `100 - i`.
    fn matching_view(source: &Tuples) -> TupleView<'_> {
        TupleView::new(
            source,
            kermit_iters::Filter::new(vec![(0, 3)], vec![]),
            vec![2, 1],
        )
    }

    /// What `partition_rows` must make of a view, worked out from the source
    /// rows alone: the output rows, their source row ids and the partition
    /// offsets, partition by partition, each in source order. `keeps` is the
    /// filter's predicate and `columns` the view's.
    fn expected_copy(
        source: &Tuples, keeps: impl Fn(&[usize]) -> bool, columns: &[usize],
    ) -> (Vec<Vec<usize>>, Vec<RowId>, Vec<usize>) {
        let (mut rows, mut origin, mut offsets) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), vec![0]);
        for p in 0..PARTITIONS {
            for (id, row) in (0..).zip(source.rows()) {
                let output: Vec<usize> = columns.iter().map(|&column| row[column]).collect();
                if keeps(row) && first_mod_3(&output) == p {
                    rows.push(output);
                    origin.push(id);
                }
            }
            offsets.push(rows.len());
        }
        (rows, origin, offsets)
    }

    /// The copy holds only the matching rows, as output rows (the view's
    /// columns, in its order), in partition order, each partition in source
    /// order; `origin` names source rows, with gaps where the filter
    /// rejected; and the copy is sized for its 14 rows exactly. The filter
    /// cuts across morsel boundaries at every size below.
    #[test]
    fn partition_rows_copies_the_matching_rows_in_output_order() {
        let source = rows_of_arity(100, 3);
        let (rows, origin, offsets) = expected_copy(&source, |row| row[0] == 3, &[2, 1]);
        // The premise: 14 rows match, in partitions of 5, 5, 4 and 0.
        assert_eq!(offsets, vec![0, 5, 10, 14, 14]);
        for t in [1, 2, 3, 8] {
            for morsel in [1, 3, 5, 100, 101] {
                let case = format!("threads {t}, morsel {morsel}");
                let out = super::partition_rows(
                    threads(t),
                    &matching_view(&source),
                    morsel,
                    PARTITIONS,
                    first_mod_3,
                );
                assert_eq!(out.offsets, offsets, "{case}");
                assert_eq!(out.tuples.to_vecs(), rows, "{case}");
                assert_eq!(out.origin, origin, "{case}");
                assert_eq!(out.tuples.arity(), 2, "{case}");
                assert_eq!(out.tuples.value_capacity(), 14 * 2, "{case}: exact size");
            }
        }
    }

    /// An equality filter and a projection to one column: `col0 = col1` holds
    /// only for `i < 7` (`i % 7 == i`), whose output rows are `[i]`.
    #[test]
    fn partition_rows_reads_an_equality_filter_and_a_projection() {
        let source = rows_of_arity(100, 3);
        let view = TupleView::new(
            &source,
            kermit_iters::Filter::new(vec![], vec![(0, 1)]),
            vec![1],
        );
        let (rows, origin, offsets) = expected_copy(&source, |row| row[0] == row[1], &[1]);
        assert_eq!(offsets, vec![0, 3, 5, 7, 7], "the premise: 7 rows match");
        for t in [1, 3] {
            for morsel in [1, 2, 3, 100] {
                let case = format!("threads {t}, morsel {morsel}");
                let out = super::partition_rows(threads(t), &view, morsel, PARTITIONS, first_mod_3);
                assert_eq!(out.offsets, offsets, "{case}");
                assert_eq!(out.tuples.to_vecs(), rows, "{case}");
                assert_eq!(out.origin, origin, "{case}");
            }
        }
    }

    /// `partition_of` runs once per matching row, on the output row, and
    /// never for a row the filter rejects.
    #[test]
    fn partition_rows_calls_partition_of_once_per_matching_row() {
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
        let source = rows_of_arity(100, 3);
        for t in [1, 3] {
            for morsel in [1, 7, 101] {
                let calls = AtomicUsize::new(0);
                let out = super::partition_rows(
                    threads(t),
                    &matching_view(&source),
                    morsel,
                    PARTITIONS,
                    |row| {
                        assert_eq!(row.len(), 2, "partition_of sees the output row");
                        calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        first_mod_3(row)
                    },
                );
                assert_eq!(calls.into_inner(), 14, "threads {t}, morsel {morsel}");
                assert_eq!(out.offsets[PARTITIONS], 14, "threads {t}, morsel {morsel}");
            }
        }
    }

    /// A view that matches nothing copies nothing, however many source rows
    /// it rejects, and still runs both passes (see `partition_rows`).
    #[test]
    fn partition_rows_of_a_view_that_matches_nothing_copies_nothing() {
        let source = rows_of_arity(10, 3);
        let view = TupleView::new(
            &source,
            kermit_iters::Filter::new(vec![(0, 99)], vec![]),
            vec![0, 1, 2],
        );
        for t in [1, 3] {
            take_worker_runs();
            let out = super::partition_rows(threads(t), &view, 4, PARTITIONS, first_mod_3);
            assert_eq!(out.offsets, vec![0; PARTITIONS + 1], "threads {t}");
            assert_eq!(
                (
                    out.tuples.arity(),
                    out.tuples.len(),
                    out.tuples.value_capacity()
                ),
                (3, 0, 0),
                "threads {t}"
            );
            assert!(out.origin.is_empty(), "threads {t}");
            assert_eq!(take_worker_runs(), vec![t, t], "threads {t}");
        }
    }
```

Replace with:

```rust
/// Copies the rows `view` selects into partition order: partition `p` holds,
/// in source order, the output rows that `partition_of` sends to `p`, which
/// must be below `partitions`, and the partitions follow one another in
/// order. A classic histogram-and-scatter radix partition, in three steps:
///
/// 1. **Histogram.** `threads` workers take morsels of `morsel_rows`
///    consecutive source rows from a shared queue, as in [`scatter_rows`]. For
///    each row of a morsel that the view matches they write its output row
///    into a scratch row, call `partition_of` on it once, keep the row's
///    partition number, and count the morsel's matching rows per partition. A
///    row the filter rejects is skipped.
/// 2. **Offsets.** The counts add up to the copy's row count, and the copy and
///    `origin` are allocated once, at exactly that size. Prefix sums over
///    (partition, morsel) pairs, partition by partition, give every pair its
///    own range of the copy: a partition's ranges lie side by side, in morsel
///    order.
/// 3. **Scatter.** The copy and `origin` are cut into those ranges with
///    `split_at_mut`, grouped by morsel. Workers take the morsels again, each
///    with its ranges and its matching rows' partition numbers, and write
///    every matching row's output columns at the front of its partition's
///    range (`TupleView::write`), its source row id into `origin` alongside.
///    The ranges are disjoint, so no write needs a lock or an atomic.
///
/// `partition_of` runs exactly once per matching row, and never for a row the
/// filter rejects: the scatter reads the numbers the histogram kept (2 bytes a
/// row, freed as each morsel is scattered) instead of calling it again. A
/// build whose `partition_of` hashes therefore hashes each row once here, as
/// it did when it partitioned ids. The scatter does ask the view which rows
/// match a second time, in the same order, to pair the rows with the numbers.
///
/// The copy does not depend on the thread count or on which worker took which
/// morsel: a partition's ranges are in morsel order, and a morsel's rows are
/// written in source order. Its buffer is sized exactly, `len · arity` values,
/// whatever spare capacity the source has. Any arity works, nullary included.
///
/// It starts workers exactly twice, one `run_workers` call per pass
/// (histogram, then scatter), each on `threads` workers, even for a view that
/// matches nothing; a caller that must start none checks for that first.
///
/// Two costs are known and accepted:
///
/// - **The zero-fill.** The copy starts zeroed, since safe Rust cannot hand out
///   uninitialised `&mut` ranges. `vec!` asks the allocator for zeroed memory
///   (`alloc_zeroed`), which costs no serial memset when the allocator hands
///   out fresh pages, as it does for a large first allocation (a reused
///   allocation may still be zeroed by the allocator), and the pages'
///   first-touch faults land in the parallel scatter.
/// - **The bookkeeping** is one count and one range per (partition, morsel)
///   pair. The `radix:K` build, a one-thread caller, gains nothing from several
///   morsels and passes the whole source as one (`view.source_rows()`): the
///   classic one-thread radix partition, one histogram and one scatter;
///   `parallel:1` and `presized:1` keep `MORSEL_TUPLES`-row morsels.
///
/// # Panics
///
/// Panics if `morsel_rows` is zero, if `partitions` exceeds 2¹⁶ (65 536, the
/// most any build uses: `radix:16`), or if `partition_of` returns
/// `partitions` or more, or panics itself.
pub(crate) fn partition_rows(
    threads: Threads, view: &TupleView<'_>, morsel_rows: usize, partitions: usize,
    partition_of: impl Fn(&[usize]) -> usize + Sync,
) -> Partitioned {
    assert!(
        morsel_rows > 0,
        "partition_rows: a morsel holds at least one row"
    );
    // A row's partition number is kept as a `u16` between the two passes, as
    // the radix build kept it before it copied the rows (#101).
    assert!(
        partitions <= 1 << 16,
        "partition_rows: at most 65,536 partitions, got {partitions}"
    );
    let (source_rows, arity) = (view.source_rows(), view.arity());
    let morsels = source_rows.div_ceil(morsel_rows);
    let morsel_ids = |m: usize| {
        let first = m * morsel_rows;
        row_id(first)..row_id(first + morsel_rows.min(source_rows - first))
    };

    // 1. Histogram: `counts[m][p]` of morsel `m`'s matching rows go to
    //    partition `p`, and `partition_numbers[m]` holds each of them
    //    partition, in row order.
    let queue = Mutex::new(0..morsels);
    let mut counts: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); morsels];
    let mut partition_numbers: Vec<Vec<u16>> = vec![Vec::new(); morsels];
    let counted = run_workers(threads, || {
        let mut counted = Vec::new();
        // One scratch row per worker: the output row `partition_of` sees.
        let mut output = vec![0; arity];
        while let Some(m) = take_next(&queue) {
            let ids = morsel_ids(m);
            let mut histogram = vec![0; partitions];
            // At most one number per row of the morsel, so it never grows.
            let mut morsel_numbers = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());
            for id in ids {
                if !view.matches(id) {
                    continue;
                }
                view.write(id, &mut output);
                let p = partition_of(&output);
                assert!(
                    p < partitions,
                    "partition_rows: partition_of returned {p} for {partitions} partitions"
                );
                histogram[p] += 1;
                // Lossless: `p < partitions <= 2^16`, by the two assertions.
                morsel_numbers.push(p as u16);
            }
            counted.push((m, histogram, morsel_numbers));
        }
        counted
    });
    for (m, histogram, morsel_numbers) in counted.into_iter().flatten() {
        counts[m] = histogram;
        partition_numbers[m] = morsel_numbers;
    }

    // 2. Offsets, and the copy cut into one range per (partition, morsel) pair,
    //    partition by partition: `ranges[m][p]` is where morsel `m` writes its
    //    rows of partition `p`. The counts add up to the copy's row count.
    //    `vec!` of zeros allocates through `alloc_zeroed`, at exactly the
    //    copy's size, so the buffer has no spare capacity. `origin` is zeroed
    //    the same way.
    let len: usize = counts.iter().flatten().sum();
    let mut values = vec![0usize; len * arity];
    let mut origin: Vec<RowId> = vec![0; len];
    let mut offsets = Vec::with_capacity(partitions + 1);
    offsets.push(0);
    {
        let mut unassigned = Cursor {
            values: values.as_mut_slice(),
            origin: origin.as_mut_slice(),
        };
        let mut ranges: Vec<Vec<Cursor<'_>>> = (0..morsels)
            .map(|_| Vec::with_capacity(partitions))
            .collect();
        let mut end = 0;
        for p in 0..partitions {
            for (morsel_ranges, morsel_counts) in ranges.iter_mut().zip(&counts) {
                let rows = morsel_counts[p];
                morsel_ranges.push(unassigned.split_off_front(rows, arity));
                end += rows;
            }
            offsets.push(end);
        }
        debug_assert_eq!(end, len, "the histograms count every row once");

        // 3. Scatter: each worker takes a morsel with its ranges and its
        //    matching rows' partition numbers, and writes every matching row
        //    at the front of its partition's range. `partition_of` is not
        //    called again; the view is asked which rows match, in the order
        //    the histogram asked it.
        let queue = Mutex::new(ranges.into_iter().zip(partition_numbers).enumerate());
        run_workers(threads, || {
            while let Some((m, (mut ranges, morsel_numbers))) = take_next(&queue) {
                let mut numbers = morsel_numbers.into_iter();
                for id in morsel_ids(m).filter(|&id| view.matches(id)) {
                    let p = numbers
                        .next()
                        .expect("the histogram numbered every matching row");
                    ranges[p as usize].write(view, id);
                }
            }
        });
        // The ranges borrow `values` and `origin` until this block ends.
    }
    Partitioned {
        tuples: Tuples::from_flat(arity, len, values),
        offsets,
        origin,
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// A `parallel:t` trie built through `HashTrie::from_view_partitioned`
    /// with morsels of 7 source rows, which make the partition step cut a
    /// small input many times.
    fn parallel_view_in_small_morsels<H: HashStrategy, P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>(
        arity: usize, config: HashTrieConfig, view: &TupleView<'_>, t: usize,
    ) -> HashTrie<H, P, E> {
        HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_view_partitioned(
            arity.into(),
            config,
            view,
            |view, links, log2, arity| {
                let mut root = HashTrie::<H, P, E>::make_root_sized(arity, log2);
                let copy = fill_root_in_morsels::<H, P, E>(
                    view,
                    links,
                    &mut root,
                    arity,
                    threads(t),
                    7,
                    config,
                );
                (copy, root)
            },
        )
    }

    /// [`parallel_view_in_small_morsels`] over a whole batch.
    fn parallel_in_small_morsels<H: HashStrategy, P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>(
        arity: usize, config: HashTrieConfig, tuples: &Tuples, t: usize,
    ) -> HashTrie<H, P, E> {
        parallel_view_in_small_morsels::<H, P, E>(arity, config, &TupleView::all(tuples), t)
    }

    /// Two filtered, permuted views of a three-column source: a constant on
    /// the third column, read as columns `[1, 0]`, and an equality of the
    /// second and third, read as columns `[2, 0, 1]`. Between them they keep
    /// no rows, some, and all of a source, so the filter cuts across morsel
    /// boundaries in the small-morsel and small-region tests.
    fn filtered_views(source: &Tuples) -> Vec<(&'static str, TupleView<'_>)> {
        vec![
            (
                "col2 = 3, columns [1, 0]",
                TupleView::new(source, Filter::new(vec![(2, 3)], vec![]), vec![1, 0]),
            ),
            (
                "col1 = col2, columns [2, 0, 1]",
                TupleView::new(source, Filter::new(vec![], vec![(1, 2)]), vec![2, 0, 1]),
            ),
        ]
    }

    /// `parallel:N` over a filtered, permuted view, in morsels of 7, builds the
    /// trie `bulk` builds from the same view, by contents, under every config
    /// and thread count, for the layout `H`, `P`, `E`.
    fn check_filtered_views_in_small_morsels<
        H: HashStrategy,
        P: PruningPolicy,
        E: ExpansionPolicy,
    >() {
        for config in configs() {
            for (input, source) in inputs(3) {
                for (name, view) in filtered_views(&source) {
                    let arity = view.arity();
                    let bulk = HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_view_with_config(
                        arity.into(),
                        config,
                        view.clone(),
                    );
                    for &t in THREADS {
                        let label = format!(
                            "{}/{}/{} {input}, {name}, root {}, load {}%, children {}, \
                             parallel:{t}, morsels of 7",
                            H::NAME,
                            P::NAME,
                            E::NAME,
                            config.root_capacity.axis_value(),
                            config.load_factor.numerator(),
                            config.child_capacity.axis_value(),
                        );
                        let small =
                            parallel_view_in_small_morsels::<H, P, E>(arity, config, &view, t);
                        assert_same_contents(&bulk, &small, &label);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn parallel_over_a_filtered_view_in_small_morsels_builds_the_bulk_trie() {
        check_filtered_views_in_small_morsels::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>();
        check_filtered_views_in_small_morsels::<SipHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, LazyExpansion>();
        check_filtered_views_in_small_morsels::<Mod10HashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>();
    }
```

Replace with:

```rust
/// Fills the empty `root` with the rows `view` selects by the `radix:bits`
/// build, threading every list through `links` (one link per matching row),
/// and returns the trie's buffer: the matching rows copied into partition
/// order. The view only borrows its source, which stays where it is. The
/// caller checks that the view's arity is `arity`.
pub(super) fn fill_root<H: HashStrategy, P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>(
    view: &TupleView<'_>, links: &ChainLinks, root: &mut HashTrieNode<P, E>, arity: usize,
    bits: RadixBits, config: HashTrieConfig,
) -> Tuples {
    if links.is_empty() {
        // No row matches (`links` holds one link per matching row). The bulk
        // build of nothing is the empty root over the empty batch: copy
        // nothing and start no worker, as `parallel:N` does.
        return Tuples::new(arity);
    }
    // 1. Partition, on this thread: copy the matching rows into `2^bits`
    //    partitions on the top `bits` of their first attribute's hash. Each
    //    partition is one range of the copy, in source order. The whole
    //    source is one morsel: `partition_rows` keeps a count and a range per
    //    (partition, morsel) pair, which one thread gains nothing from, and
    //    at `radix:16` over 10^7 rows in `MORSEL_TUPLES`-row morsels would be
    //    about 40 million pairs. The copy is the trie's buffer from here on.
    let one = Threads::new(1).expect("one thread is a valid count");
    let one_morsel = view.source_rows();
    let partitioned = partition_by_first_hash::<H>(one, view, one_morsel, u32::from(bits.get()));
    // 2 and 3, on this thread.
    build_and_merge::<H, P, E>(partitioned, links, root, arity, one, config)
}

/// Step 1 of `radix:K` and `parallel:N`: copies the rows `view` selects into
/// `2^bits` partitions on the top `bits` bits of their first attribute's
/// hash, each partition's rows in source order, with each copied row's source
/// row id in `origin` (`morsel::partition_rows`, on `threads` workers over
/// morsels of `morsel_rows` source rows). `bits` must be in `1..=16`.
pub(super) fn partition_by_first_hash<H: HashStrategy>(
    threads: Threads, view: &TupleView<'_>, morsel_rows: usize, bits: u32,
) -> Partitioned {
    debug_assert!(
        (1..=16).contains(&bits),
        "partition_by_first_hash: {bits} bits, not 1 to 16"
    );
    let shift = 64 - bits;
    partition_rows(threads, view, morsel_rows, 1 << bits, |row| {
        (H::hash(row[0]) >> shift) as usize
    })
}
```

```rust
/// Fills the empty `root` with the rows `view` selects by the
/// `parallel:threads` build, threading every list through `links` (one link
/// per matching row), and returns the partitioned copy of those rows that
/// the trie keeps as its buffer: every id in `root` names a row of it. The
/// view only borrows its source, which stays where it is. The caller checks
/// that the view's arity is `arity`.
pub(super) fn fill_root<H: HashStrategy, P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>(
    view: &TupleView<'_>, links: &ChainLinks, root: &mut HashTrieNode<P, E>, arity: usize,
    threads: Threads, config: HashTrieConfig,
) -> Tuples {
    fill_root_in_morsels::<H, P, E>(view, links, root, arity, threads, MORSEL_TUPLES, config)
}

/// [`fill_root`] with the morsel size as a parameter, so tests can cut a
/// small input into many morsels.
fn fill_root_in_morsels<H: HashStrategy, P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>(
    view: &TupleView<'_>, links: &ChainLinks, root: &mut HashTrieNode<P, E>, arity: usize,
    threads: Threads, morsel_tuples: usize, config: HashTrieConfig,
) -> Tuples {
    if links.is_empty() {
        // No row matches (`links` holds one link per matching row). The bulk
        // build of nothing is the empty root over the empty batch: copy
        // nothing and start no worker.
        return Tuples::new(arity);
    }
    // 1. Partition, on `threads` workers, by the top bits of each row's first
    //    attribute's hash. The matching rows are copied into partition order,
    //    each partition's in source order, with each copy's source row id in
    //    `origin`. The copy is the trie's buffer from here on.
    let partitioned = radix::partition_by_first_hash::<H>(
        threads,
        view,
        morsel_tuples,
        partition_bits(threads),
    );
```

```rust
    /// What the partitioned builds share (`radix:K`, `parallel:N`,

    /// root over the batch at the capacity every build gives it

    pub(super) fn from_tuples_partitioned(

        fill: impl FnOnce(Tuples, &ChainLinks, u32, usize) -> (Tuples, HashTrieNode<P, E>),
```

```rust
    /// What the partitioned builds share (`radix:K`, `parallel:N`,
    /// `presized:N`): the view's arity check, then `fill`, which builds the
    /// root over the view at the capacity every build gives it
    /// (`HashTrieConfig::root_log2_capacity` of the rows the view matches,
    /// presized under `root-capacity=tuples`) and returns it with the trie's
    /// buffer: the matching rows copied into partition order
    /// (`morsel::partition_rows`, #101). The view only borrows its source, so
    /// that copy is the build's one. `fill` threads the rows of that buffer
    /// through `links`, one per matching row (`view.count()` of them),
    /// zeroed: every fill writes a row's link before it reads it, and starts
    /// with an empty `links` when no row matches. Tests in `parallel.rs`
    /// call it with small morsels and regions.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics as `relation::check_view_arity` does, the one check of every
    /// structure: if the view's source holds rows and the view's arity is not
    /// `header.arity()`, whether or not any row passes the filter.
    pub(super) fn from_view_partitioned(
        header: RelationHeader, config: HashTrieConfig, view: &TupleView<'_>,
        fill: impl FnOnce(&TupleView<'_>, &ChainLinks, u32, usize) -> (Tuples, HashTrieNode<P, E>),
    ) -> Self {
        crate::relation::check_view_arity(&header, view);
        let arity = header.arity();
        let count = view.count();
        let log2_capacity = config.root_log2_capacity(count);
        let links = ChainLinks::new(count);
        let (tuples, root) = fill(view, &links, log2_capacity, arity);
        debug_assert_eq!(links.len(), tuples.len(), "one link per row of the buffer");
        Self {
            header,
            tuples,
            links,
            root,
            config,
            _layout: PhantomData,
        }
    }
```

The dispatch of Task 5.1 reads the view in the partitioning arms. Replace the doc comment and
body of `from_view_with_config_and_build_mode`, from the first line of its doc comment (the
sentence that begins "Creates a trie holding") through the closing `}` of that function. The
signature is unchanged (it is repeated below), and so is `batch_from_view`, which follows it
(the arity check is `relation::check_view_arity`, which `batch_from_view` and
`from_view_partitioned` call; HashTrie has no copy of it):

```rust
    /// Creates a trie holding `config`, populated with the rows `view`
    /// selects and built by `mode`: the view-reading form of
    /// [`from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode`](Self::from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode),
    /// and the constructor every `from_view*` ends in: the trait method
    /// `ConfiguredBuildModeRelation::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode`
    /// delegates to it, and so do `from_view`, `from_view_with_config` and
    /// `from_view_with_build_mode`. This `match` is the home of every mode's
    /// build. Each mode copies the matching rows once, in output-column
    /// order, into a buffer of exactly their size, and builds over that
    /// buffer:
    /// - `bulk` and `incremental` materialise the view
    ///   (`TupleView::materialize`) and keep that buffer as the trie's own;
    /// - `radix:K`, `parallel:N` and `presized:N` copy the rows into
    ///   partition order straight from the view (`morsel::partition_rows`,
    ///   #101) and keep that copy.
    ///
    /// The root is sized by the number of matching rows, never by the
    /// source's.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if the view's source holds rows and the view's arity is not
    /// `header.arity()`, whether or not any row passes the view's filter; if
    /// `mode` is `Presized` and `config.root_capacity` is not
    /// [`RootCapacity::Tuples`], or if `mode` is `Incremental` and
    /// `config.child_capacity` is not [`ChildCapacity::Grow`]: each mode's
    /// prerequisite.
    pub fn from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
        header: RelationHeader, config: HashTrieConfig, mode: HashTrieBuildMode,
        view: TupleView<'_>,
    ) -> Self {
        match mode {
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk => {
                let batch = Self::batch_from_view(&header, &view);
                Self::from_tuples_in_bulk(header, config, batch)
            },
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental => {
                Self::assert_incremental_prerequisite(config);
                let batch = Self::batch_from_view(&header, &view);
                Self::from_tuples_incrementally(header, config, batch)
            },
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Radix(bits) => {
                Self::from_view_partitioned(header, config, &view, |view, links, log2, arity| {
                    let mut root = Self::make_root_sized(arity, log2);
                    let copy =
                        radix::fill_root::<H, P, E>(view, links, &mut root, arity, bits, config);
                    (copy, root)
                })
            },
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Parallel(threads) => {
                Self::from_view_partitioned(header, config, &view, |view, links, log2, arity| {
                    let mut root = Self::make_root_sized(arity, log2);
                    let copy = parallel::fill_root::<H, P, E>(
                        view, links, &mut root, arity, threads, config,
                    );
                    (copy, root)
                })
            },
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Presized(threads) => {
                // The prerequisite
                // (docs/specs/2026-10-07-dependent-optimisations-design.md):
                // the regions are cut from a root sized before any tuple
                // arrives. The CLI rejects the pair first; here it is a
                // broken invariant, like a wrong arity.
                assert_eq!(
                    config.root_capacity,
                    RootCapacity::Tuples,
                    "hash-trie=presized:{} requires root-capacity=tuples; got root-capacity={}",
                    threads.get(),
                    config.root_capacity.axis_value(),
                );
                Self::from_view_partitioned(header, config, &view, |view, links, log2, arity| {
                    parallel::fill_presized_root::<H, P, E>(
                        view, links, log2, arity, threads, config,
                    )
                })
            },
        }
    }
```

```rust
    /// The three partitioning modes, on thread and bit counts small enough to
    /// spread a small input over several partitions.
    fn partition_modes() -> [HashTrieBuildMode; 3] {
        let threads = Threads::new(2).expect("two is a valid thread count");
        [
            HashTrieBuildMode::Radix(RadixBits::new(3).expect("three is a valid bit count")),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Parallel(threads),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Presized(threads),
        ]
    }

    /// Every build mode builds an equivalent trie from a filtered, permuted
    /// view (Amendment 2), each against `bulk` built from the view's
    /// hand-made batch: `bulk` and `incremental` array for array, `radix:K`
    /// and `parallel:N` by contents (the same tables bucket for bucket, the
    /// same tuples in every chain, the same exactly sized buffer, under the
    /// copy's row ids), `presized:N` by equivalence. `incremental` runs under
    /// the configs that accept it (children that grow) and `presized:N` under
    /// the ones that accept it (a presized root), for the layout `H`, `P`, `E`.
    fn check_modes_agree_on_views<H: HashStrategy, P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>() {
        let [radix_mode, parallel_mode, presized_mode] = partition_modes();
        for (input, source) in sources() {
            for case in cases() {
                let arity = case.columns.len();
                let expected = reference(&source, &case);
                for config in configs() {
                    let bulk = HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_tuples_with_config(
                        arity.into(),
                        config,
                        expected.clone(),
                    );
                    let mut modes = vec![HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk, radix_mode, parallel_mode];
                    if config.child_capacity == ChildCapacity::Grow {
                        modes.push(HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental);
                    }
                    if config.root_capacity == RootCapacity::Tuples {
                        modes.push(presized_mode);
                    }
                    for mode in modes {
                        let label = format!(
                            "{}/{}/{} {input}, {}, load {}%, root {}, children {}, {mode:?}",
                            H::NAME,
                            P::NAME,
                            E::NAME,
                            case.name,
                            config.load_factor.numerator(),
                            config.root_capacity.axis_value(),
                            config.child_capacity.axis_value(),
                        );
                        let view =
                            TupleView::new(&source, case.filter.clone(), case.columns.clone());
                        let built = HashTrie::<H, P, E>::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
                            arity.into(),
                            config,
                            mode,
                            view,
                        );
                        match mode {
                            | HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk | HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental => {
                                assert_same_trie(&bulk, &built, &label)
                            },
                            | HashTrieBuildMode::Radix(_) | HashTrieBuildMode::Parallel(_) => {
                                assert_same_contents(&bulk, &built, &label)
                            },
                            | HashTrieBuildMode::Presized(_) => {
                                assert_equivalent_trie(&bulk, &built, &label)
                            },
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_build_mode_builds_an_equivalent_trie_from_a_view() {
        check_modes_agree_on_views::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>();
        check_modes_agree_on_views::<FxHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, EagerExpansion>();
        check_modes_agree_on_views::<SipHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, LazyExpansion>();
    }

    /// A view that matches no row builds the empty trie in every
    /// partitioning mode, without partitioning or starting a worker, though
    /// its source holds rows. (`radix_build_of_nothing_starts_no_worker` is
    /// the same for an empty source.)
    #[test]
    fn a_view_that_matches_nothing_starts_no_worker() {
        let source = hand_source();
        let config = HashTrieConfig {
            root_capacity: RootCapacity::Tuples,
            ..HashTrieConfig::default()
        };
        let empty: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_tuples_with_config(2.into(), config, vec![]);
        for mode in partition_modes() {
            crate::morsel::take_worker_runs();
            let view = TupleView::new(&source, Filter::new(vec![(0, 99)], vec![]), vec![0, 1]);
            let built: HashTrie =
                HashTrie::from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(2.into(), config, mode, view);
            assert_same_trie(&empty, &built, &format!("{mode:?}"));
            assert!(
                crate::morsel::take_worker_runs().is_empty(),
                "{mode:?}: a worker ran"
            );
        }
    }
```

## Story 7: Views become the one build path

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit-ds/src/relation.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/configured.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/built_with.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/tree_trie/implementation.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/column_trie/implementation.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/hash_trie/implementation.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/hash_trie/identity.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/ds/hash_trie/bulk.rs`, `kermit/tests/tuple_allocation.rs`
- **Interfaces:** makes Story 2's `from_view*` the required constructors and every `from_tuples*` a provided one; every later build goes through them
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit --test tuple_allocation`
- **Review:** deep

Stories 2 to 6 gave every structure a view build beside its tuple build, and left the
`from_view*` constructors with bridge defaults that materialise the view and call the tuple
constructors. This story removes the bridge. `from_view`, `from_view_with_config`,
`from_view_with_build_mode` and `from_view_with_config_and_build_mode` become required, and
the four `from_tuples*` constructors become provided methods that convert their argument to
a `Tuples` batch and call the matching `from_view*` with `TupleView::all`. Each structure's
own `from_tuples*` methods are deleted, so tests, loaders and benchmarks run the one build
path. `read_csv`'s comment stops saying that `HashTrie` keeps the reader's buffer, since
every build now copies from a view, so HashTrie's tuple-path helpers (`from_tuples_in_bulk`,
`from_tuples_incrementally`, `batch_for_header`) go and its inherent `from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode`
shrinks to a delegation; the tests that called them, and the `identity.rs` test that relied on a
batch's spare capacity, are reworked. `tuple_allocation.rs` gains view-build cells: a filtered,
projected and permuted view builds every structure and build mode without allocating per
input row, including per skipped row. The tree stays green after the one code task because
the compiler checks that no structure still relies on a bridge, and the second task only
adds tests. No code here holds a landmine marker.

```rust
    // ── from_tuples* are provided over from_view* ──────────────────────

    /// A configuration value for [`ViewOnly`].
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
    struct ViewOnlyConfig(u8);

    /// A relation that implements only the `from_view*` constructors and

    #[derive(Debug)]

    }

    impl ViewOnly {
        fn record(
            header: RelationHeader, config: ViewOnlyConfig, mode: Option<ViewOnlyMode>,
            view: &kermit_iters::TupleView<'_>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self {
                header,
                rows: view.materialize().to_vecs(),
                identity: view.is_identity(),
                source_rows: view.source_rows(),
                config,
                mode,
            }
        }

    impl JoinIterable for ViewOnly {}

            unimplemented!("ViewOnly is never projected")
        }
    }

    impl Relation for ViewOnly {
        fn header(&self) -> &RelationHeader { &self.header }

        fn new(header: RelationHeader) -> Self {
            let empty = Tuples::new(header.arity());
            Self::record(
                header,
                ViewOnlyConfig::default(),
                None,
                &kermit_iters::TupleView::all(&empty),
            )
        }

        fn from_view(header: RelationHeader, view: kermit_iters::TupleView<'_>) -> Self {
            Self::record(header, ViewOnlyConfig::default(), None, &view)
        }

        fn insert(&mut self, tuple: impl AsRef<[usize]>) {
            self.rows.push(tuple.as_ref().to_vec());
        }

        fn insert_all(&mut self, tuples: impl Into<Tuples>) {
            let tuples: Tuples = tuples.into();
            self.rows.extend(tuples.to_vecs());
        }
    }

    impl ConfigurableRelation for ViewOnly {
        type Config = ViewOnlyConfig;

        fn with_config(header: RelationHeader, config: ViewOnlyConfig) -> Self {
            let mut relation = Self::new(header);
            relation.config = config;
            relation
        }

        fn from_view_with_config(
            header: RelationHeader, config: ViewOnlyConfig, view: kermit_iters::TupleView<'_>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self::record(header, config, None, &view)
        }

        fn config(&self) -> &ViewOnlyConfig { &self.config }
    }

    impl BuildModeRelation for ViewOnly {
        type BuildMode = ViewOnlyMode;

        fn from_view_with_build_mode(
            header: RelationHeader, mode: ViewOnlyMode, view: kermit_iters::TupleView<'_>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self::record(header, ViewOnlyConfig::default(), Some(mode), &view)
        }
    }

    impl ConfiguredBuildModeRelation for ViewOnly {
        fn from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(
            header: RelationHeader, config: ViewOnlyConfig, mode: ViewOnlyMode,
            view: kermit_iters::TupleView<'_>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self::record(header, config, Some(mode), &view)
        }
    }

    /// Each `from_tuples*` converts its argument to one batch and calls the
    /// matching `from_view*` with the identity view over it: the whole batch,
    /// duplicates and all, with the config and mode the caller named.
    #[test]
    fn every_from_tuples_constructor_is_the_from_view_one_over_all() {
        let rows = vec![vec![1, 2], vec![3, 4], vec![1, 2]];
        let batch = || Tuples::from(rows.clone());

        let plain = ViewOnly::from_tuples(2.into(), batch());
        let configured = ViewOnly::from_tuples_with_config(2.into(), ViewOnlyConfig(7), batch());
        let moded =
            ViewOnly::from_tuples_with_build_mode(2.into(), ViewOnlyMode::Fancy, rows.clone());
        let both = ViewOnly::from_tuples_with_config_and_build_mode(
            2.into(),
            ViewOnlyConfig(7),
            ViewOnlyMode::Fancy,
            batch(),
        );

        for (built, config, mode) in [
            (&plain, ViewOnlyConfig(0), None),
            (&configured, ViewOnlyConfig(7), None),
            (&moded, ViewOnlyConfig(0), Some(ViewOnlyMode::Fancy)),
            (&both, ViewOnlyConfig(7), Some(ViewOnlyMode::Fancy)),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(built.rows, rows);
            assert!(built.identity, "the view is TupleView::all over the batch");
            assert_eq!(built.source_rows, 3);
            assert_eq!(built.config, config);
            assert_eq!(built.mode, mode);
            assert_eq!(built.header().arity(), 2);
        }
    }

    /// An empty literal (`vec![]`) converts to a batch of no rows, which
    /// reaches `from_view` as a view over an empty source, under any header.
    #[test]
    fn an_empty_literal_reaches_from_view_as_an_empty_source() {
        let built = ViewOnly::from_tuples(2.into(), vec![]);
        assert_eq!(built.source_rows, 0);
        assert!(built.rows.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(built.header().arity(), 2);
    }
```

```rust
    /// Creates a relation from the rows `view` keeps, matching `header`.
    ///
    /// The one required constructor: every `from_tuples*` method is this one
    /// over [`TupleView::all`]. The relation reads the view's matching rows,
    /// in its output-column order, and copies them once into the structure it
    /// builds, so no build allocates per input row. Implementations may sort
    /// or deduplicate during bulk construction; prefer this over `new`
    /// followed by repeated `insert` calls when all tuples are known up
    /// front. A view over an empty source builds an empty relation under any
    /// header.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics with `from_tuples: tuple arity {view.arity()} does not match
    /// header arity {header.arity()}` if the view's source holds rows and
    /// `view.arity()` does not equal `header.arity()`.
    fn from_view(header: RelationHeader, view: TupleView<'_>) -> Self;

    /// Creates a relation populated with `tuples`, matching `header`: the
    /// identity view over the batch ([`TupleView::all`]) given to
    /// [`from_view`](Self::from_view), after which the batch is dropped.
    /// `tuples` is a [`Tuples`] batch, or anything that converts into one:
    /// test fixtures pass one `Vec<usize>` per tuple, whose conversion
    /// panics on mixed arity. An empty batch is accepted under any header.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// As [`from_view`](Self::from_view) for a non-empty batch whose arity
    /// does not equal `header.arity()`. A `Vec<Vec<usize>>` of mixed
    /// arities panics earlier, while converting to [`Tuples`].
    fn from_tuples(header: RelationHeader, tuples: impl Into<Tuples>) -> Self
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        let tuples: Tuples = tuples.into();
        Self::from_view(header, TupleView::all(&tuples))
    }
```

```rust
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk => {
                let batch = Self::batch_from_view(&header, &view);
                Self::from_tuples_in_bulk(header, config, batch)
            },
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental => {
                Self::assert_incremental_prerequisite(config);
                let batch = Self::batch_from_view(&header, &view);
                Self::from_tuples_incrementally(header, config, batch)
            },
```

with

```rust
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk => {
                // Algorithm 2 from the root (`bulk.rs`) over every row id of the
                // copy, in input order, the root sized as every build sizes it,
                // by `HashTrieConfig::root_log2_capacity` (#88). The trie keeps
                // the copy as its buffer and threads its rows through one link
                // each. The links start zeroed (`ChainLinks::new`): the root's
                // grouping writes every row's link before any is read.
                #[cfg(test)]
                BULK_BUILDS.with(|n| n.set(n.get() + 1));
                let arity = header.arity();
                let tuples = Self::batch_from_view(&header, &view);
                let log2_capacity = config.root_log2_capacity(tuples.len());
                let links = ChainLinks::new(tuples.len());
                let root = Self::build(
                    &tuples,
                    &links,
                    0,
                    arity,
                    all_rows(&tuples),
                    log2_capacity,
                    config,
                );
                Self {
                    header,
                    tuples,
                    links,
                    root,
                    config,
                    _layout: PhantomData,
                }
            },
            | HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental => {
                // One `insert_at` per row, in input order: the build
                // `from_tuples_with_config` ran before #107.
                Self::assert_incremental_prerequisite(config);
                let arity = header.arity();
                let tuples = Self::batch_from_view(&header, &view);
                let mut trie = Self::with_config_for(header, config, tuples);
                for row in all_rows(&trie.tuples) {
                    // As `insert` does: a row's link is `NIL` until a chain
                    // threads it, so a row that stays a pruned `Singleton`
                    // holds `NIL`, as `bulk` leaves it. (Zeroed links would
                    // leave it at 0.)
                    trie.links.push(ChainLinks::NIL);
                    Self::insert_at(
                        &trie.tuples,
                        &trie.links,
                        &mut trie.root,
                        0,
                        arity,
                        row,
                        config.load_factor,
                    );
                }
                trie
            },
```

`same_contents_rejects_another_buffer_capacity` built one trie from a batch with spare
capacity and relied on `from_tuples` keeping that batch. Every build now copies its rows
at their exact size, so both tries would have the same capacity and the test would stop
panicking. Build the second trie by `insert` instead, which grows its buffer past the
rows' size. Replace

```rust
    /// The same trie over a buffer with spare capacity: equal nodes and

    #[test]

        let exact = rows(2, &INTERLEAVED);
        let mut spare = Tuples::with_capacity(2, 64);
        for row in exact.rows() {
            spare.push(row);
        }
        let a: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_tuples(2.into(), exact);
        let b: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_tuples(2.into(), spare);
        assert_same_contents(&a, &b, "spare");
    }
```

```rust
    /// The same trie over a buffer with spare capacity: equal nodes and
    /// rows, another capacity. Every build copies its rows at their exact
    /// size, so the spare capacity comes from growing the buffer by `insert`,
    /// which doubles it past the rows' size; the nodes are the build's, since
    /// the `incremental` build is `insert` in input order.
    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "buffer capacity")]
    fn same_contents_rejects_another_buffer_capacity() {
        let exact: HashTrie = HashTrie::from_tuples(2.into(), rows(2, &INTERLEAVED));
        let mut grown: HashTrie = HashTrie::new(2.into());
        grown.insert_all(rows(2, &INTERLEAVED));
        assert!(
            grown.tuples().value_capacity() > exact.tuples().value_capacity(),
            "the premise: inserting grows the buffer past its exact size"
        );
        assert_same_contents(&exact, &grown, "spare");
    }
```

In the doc comment above `hash_trie_presized_build_allocates_independently_of_its_row_count`,
Story 6 renamed `from_tuples_partitioned` to `from_view_partitioned`, so fix the comment
that names it. Replace

```rust

/// allocates once at the row count. Its partitions are whole runs of the
```

with

```rust
/// threaded through the trie's links, which `from_view_partitioned`
```
