
Append to the end of the file (after `hash_trie_presized_build_allocates_independently_of_its_row_count`):

```rust

// ── Builds from views ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// What column 2 holds in the rows a view keeps.
const KEPT: usize = 7;
/// What column 2 holds in the decoy rows the view rejects.
const DECOY: usize = 8;

/// The view every cell below builds from: the rows whose column 2 is [`KEPT`],
/// read as `(column 1, column 0)`. A filter, a projection and a permutation
/// at once, so the build must apply all three while it copies.
fn kept_rows(source: &Tuples) -> TupleView<'_> {
    TupleView::new(source, Filter::new(vec![(2, KEPT)], vec![]), vec![1, 0])
}

/// [`fanned_out`]'s rows hidden in a wider batch: each `(x, y)` is stored as
/// `(y, x, KEPT)`, in the same descending order, and every fourth `x` also
/// stores a decoy `(y, FIRST_KEYS + x, DECOY)` whose output row is a key the
/// fixture lacks. 12 500 rows, so a one-thread parallel build still sees one
/// 16 384-row morsel; a build that ignored the filter would store 2 500 more
/// distinct rows.
fn fanned_out_in_decoys() -> Tuples {
    let mut tuples = Tuples::with_capacity(
        3,
        FIRST_KEYS * FAN_OUT + FIRST_KEYS.div_ceil(4) * FAN_OUT,
    );
    for x in (0..FIRST_KEYS).rev() {
        for y in (0..FAN_OUT).rev() {
            tuples.push(&[y, x, KEPT]);
            if x % 4 == 0 {
                tuples.push(&[y, FIRST_KEYS + x, DECOY]);
            }
        }
    }
    tuples
}

/// [`repeated`]'s rows hidden in a wider batch: each `(x, y)` is stored as
/// `(y, x, KEPT)`, in the same order, and the first repetition also stores
/// a decoy `(y, x, DECOY)` after each. The decoys are 100 rows at either
/// repetition, so the larger source stays inside one 16 384-row morsel, and a
/// build that ignored the filter would store 100 rows too many.
fn repeated_in_decoys(repeats: usize) -> Tuples {
    let mut tuples = Tuples::with_capacity(3, (repeats + 1) * KEYS * KEYS);
    for repeat in 0..repeats {
        for x in 0..KEYS {
            for y in 0..KEYS {
                tuples.push(&[y, x, KEPT]);
                if repeat == 0 {
                    tuples.push(&[y, x, DECOY]);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    tuples
}

/// [`tree_trie_build_allocates_once_per_inner_node`] for a build from
/// [`kept_rows`]: the same trie from the same output rows, so the same bound.
/// `serial` copies the kept rows once into the batch it sorts.
#[test]
fn tree_trie_build_from_a_filtered_view_allocates_once_per_inner_node() {
    let source = fanned_out_in_decoys();
    let view = kept_rows(&source);
    let rows = FIRST_KEYS * FAN_OUT;
    assert_eq!(view.count(), rows, "the view keeps the fanned-out rows and no decoy");
    assert!(source.len() > rows, "the source holds decoys the build must skip");
    let mut built: Option<TreeTrie> = None;
    let info = allocation_counter::measure(|| built = Some(TreeTrie::from_view(2.into(), view)));
    assert_eq!(built.expect("measured").tuple_count(), rows);
    let nodes = FIRST_KEYS as u64 + doublings(FIRST_KEYS);
    assert!(
        info.count_total <= nodes + SCRATCH,
        "TreeTrie from a view: {} allocations for {rows} rows; its inner nodes account for \
         {nodes}",
        info.count_total
    );
}

/// [`tree_trie_parallel_build_on_one_thread_allocates_per_partition_not_per_row`]
/// for a build from [`kept_rows`]: the workers gather the kept rows of their
/// partitions out of the view, and the row-id buckets hold only kept rows.
#[test]
fn tree_trie_parallel_view_build_on_one_thread_allocates_per_partition_not_per_row() {
    let source = fanned_out_in_decoys();
    let view = kept_rows(&source);
    let rows = FIRST_KEYS * FAN_OUT;
    assert_eq!(view.count(), rows, "the view keeps the fanned-out rows and no decoy");
    let mode = TreeTrieBuildMode::Parallel(one_thread());
    let mut built: Option<TreeTrie> = None;
    let info = allocation_counter::measure(|| {
        built = Some(TreeTrie::from_view_with_build_mode(2.into(), mode, view));
    });
    assert_eq!(built.expect("measured").tuple_count(), rows);
    let builds = take_tree_trie_parallel_builds();
    assert!(
        matches!(builds.as_slice(), [(1, _)]),
        "parallel:1 ran one build on one thread: {builds:?}"
    );
    let nodes = FIRST_KEYS as u64 + doublings(FIRST_KEYS);
    let partitions = ONE_THREAD_PARTITIONS * (doublings(rows) + 1 + 1 + doublings(FIRST_KEYS));
    let bound = nodes + partitions + ONE_THREAD_MACHINERY + SCRATCH;
    assert!(
        info.count_total <= bound,
        "TreeTrie parallel:1 from a view: {} allocations for {rows} rows, over {bound}: its inner \
         nodes account for {nodes} and its partitions for {partitions}",
        info.count_total
    );
}

/// [`column_trie_builds_allocate_only_their_layer_arrays`] for a build from
/// [`kept_rows`], under both build modes.
#[test]
fn column_trie_view_builds_allocate_only_their_layer_arrays() {
    for mode in [ColumnTrieBuildMode::Bulk, ColumnTrieBuildMode::Incremental] {
        let source = fanned_out_in_decoys();
        let view = kept_rows(&source);
        let rows = FIRST_KEYS * FAN_OUT;
        assert_eq!(view.count(), rows, "the view keeps the fanned-out rows and no decoy");
        let mut built: Option<ColumnTrie> = None;
        let info = allocation_counter::measure(|| {
            built = Some(ColumnTrie::from_view_with_build_mode(2.into(), mode, view));
        });
        assert_eq!(built.expect("measured").tuple_count(), rows, "{mode:?}");
        let arrays = 1 + 2 * 2 * doublings(rows);
        assert!(
            info.count_total <= arrays + SCRATCH,
            "ColumnTrie {mode:?} from a view: {} allocations for {rows} rows; its layer arrays \
             account for {arrays}",
            info.count_total
        );
    }
}

/// [`measure_hash_build`] for a build from [`kept_rows`] over
/// [`repeated_in_decoys`]: the same trie as `repeated(repeats)` builds, so
/// the stored row count (a multiset's, decoys excluded) is `repeats × 100`.
fn measure_hash_view_build<P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>(
    config: HashTrieConfig, mode: HashTrieBuildMode, repeats: usize,
) -> (u64, Vec<HashTrieParallelBuild>) {
    let source = repeated_in_decoys(repeats);
    let view = kept_rows(&source);
    let rows = repeats * KEYS * KEYS;
    assert_eq!(view.count(), rows, "the view keeps the repeated rows and no decoy");
    assert!(source.len() > rows, "the source holds decoys the build must skip");
    let mut built: Option<HashTrie<SipHashStrategy, P, E>> = None;
    let info = allocation_counter::measure(|| {
        built = Some(
            <HashTrie<SipHashStrategy, P, E> as ConfiguredBuildModeRelation>::
                from_view_with_config_and_build_mode(2.into(), config, mode, view),
        );
    });
    assert_eq!(built.expect("measured").tuple_count(), rows);
    (info.count_total, take_hash_trie_parallel_builds())
}

/// [`hash_build_allocations`] for a build from a view.
fn hash_view_build_allocations<P: PruningPolicy, E: ExpansionPolicy>(
    mode: HashTrieBuildMode, repeats: usize,
) -> u64 {
    let (allocations, builds) =
        measure_hash_view_build::<P, E>(HashTrieConfig::default(), mode, repeats);
    let threads: Vec<usize> = builds.iter().map(|build| build.threads).collect();
    let expected = match mode {
        | HashTrieBuildMode::Parallel(threads) => vec![threads.get()],
        | _ => vec![],
    };
    assert_eq!(threads, expected, "{mode:?}: the parallel builds that ran");
    allocations
}

/// [`hash_trie_builds_allocate_independently_of_their_row_count`] for builds
/// from a filtered view: ten times as many kept rows may not cost a single
/// allocation more, in any build mode. The copy is sized once from the view's
/// count, and the decoys, rejected in the counting and scatter passes, cost
/// nothing.
#[test]
fn hash_trie_view_builds_allocate_independently_of_their_row_count() {
    let radix = HashTrieBuildMode::Radix(RadixBits::new(2).unwrap());
    type Measure = fn(HashTrieBuildMode, usize) -> u64;
    let cells: [(&str, Measure, HashTrieBuildMode); 5] = [
        (
            "eager",
            hash_view_build_allocations::<NoPruning, EagerExpansion>,
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
        ),
        (
            "pruned lazy",
            hash_view_build_allocations::<SingletonPruning, LazyExpansion>,
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
        ),
        (
            "eager",
            hash_view_build_allocations::<NoPruning, EagerExpansion>,
            HashTrieBuildMode::Incremental,
        ),
        (
            "eager",
            hash_view_build_allocations::<NoPruning, EagerExpansion>,
            radix,
        ),
        (
            "eager",
            hash_view_build_allocations::<NoPruning, EagerExpansion>,
            HashTrieBuildMode::Parallel(one_thread()),
        ),
    ];
    for (layout, allocations, mode) in cells {
        let (once, many) = (allocations(mode, 1), allocations(mode, REPEATS));
        assert!(
            many <= once,
            "HashTrie {layout} {mode:?} from a view: {once} allocations for {} kept rows, {many} \
             for {}: the larger build allocates more, so some row or list allocates",
            KEYS * KEYS,
            REPEATS * KEYS * KEYS
        );
    }
}

/// [`hash_trie_presized_build_allocates_independently_of_its_row_count`] for
/// a build from a filtered view. The root is sized from `view.count()`, the
/// kept rows, so the partition counts are the unfiltered fixture's: one for
/// 100 rows, four for 10 000.
#[test]
fn hash_trie_presized_view_build_allocates_independently_of_its_row_count() {
    let config = HashTrieConfig {
        root_capacity: RootCapacity::Tuples,
        ..HashTrieConfig::default()
    };
    let mode = HashTrieBuildMode::Presized(one_thread());
    let measure = |repeats| {
        let (allocations, builds) =
            measure_hash_view_build::<NoPruning, EagerExpansion>(config, mode, repeats);
        let [build] = builds.as_slice() else {
            panic!("presized:1 ran one build: {builds:?}");
        };
        assert_eq!(build.threads, 1, "presized:1 ran on one thread");
        assert_eq!(build.deferred, Some(0), "no row is deferred to the tail");
        (allocations, build.partition_sizes.len())
    };
    let ((once, once_partitions), (many, many_partitions)) = (measure(1), measure(REPEATS));
    assert_eq!((once_partitions, many_partitions), (1, 4));
    let rows = REPEATS * KEYS * KEYS;
    assert!(
        many <= once,
        "HashTrie presized:1 from a view: {once} allocations for {} kept rows, {many} for \
         {rows}: the larger build allocates more, so some row or list allocates",
        KEYS * KEYS,
    );
}
```

## Story 8: Free the names the new pipeline takes

- **Developer:** junior-dev
- **Files:** `kermit-algos/src/orient.rs`, `kermit-algos/src/lib.rs`, `kermit/src/db.rs`, `kermit/src/db/database.rs`, `kermit/src/db/validation.rs`, `kermit/src/execution.rs`, `kermit/src/bench/run.rs`, `kermit/tests/common/utils.rs`, `kermit/tests/column_orders_any.rs`, `kermit/tests/tuple_allocation.rs`
- **Interfaces:** frees `IndexSpec` for Story 10 and `prepare` / `Prepared` for Story 12 (Names contract: kermit-algos, kermit::db)
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit-algos -p kermit --no-run`
- **Review:** light (mechanical rename, no landmine)

This is a pure rename with no change in behaviour. `kermit_algos::IndexSpec` (a column-permuted
copy of a relation, used by `orient`) becomes `CopySpec` in `orient.rs`, in the facade and at
every use, so Story 10 can define its own `IndexSpec`. The private
`validation::{prepare, Prepared}` become `{check_and_rewrite, Rewritten}`, so Story 12 can
define the public `kermit::db::{prepare, Prepared}`. Nothing else changes: field names such as
`index_specs`, the `Index_` prefix, `describe` and every message stay as they are. The renames
move names within `use` lists, so each task ends with `cargo fmt`, which reorders them. No
code in this story holds a landmine marker.

## Story 9: Access extraction

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit-algos/src/access.rs`, `kermit-algos/src/lib.rs`
- **Interfaces:** exposes `Access`, `AccessQuery`, `extract_accesses` and `ACCESS_PREFIX` to Stories 10, 12, 20 and 22; uses Story 1's `Filter` and `const_rewrite::RewriteError`
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit-algos --lib access`
- **Review:** deep

`extract_accesses` walks each body atom's terms after the placeholder rewrite and turns the atom into an `Access`: a variable's first occurrence is a kept column, a later occurrence becomes an equality with that first column, and a constant becomes a constant filter. An atom with no kept column (only constants) becomes a check. The access query names the accesses `@<k>`, `k` being the position in `AccessQuery::accesses`, and its body holds one atom per access over the access's variables. This is the replacement for the const, placeholder-follow-up and selection rewrites: the filter is applied when the index is copied, so the executors never see a constant or a repeated variable. The story adds a module and a facade line only; nothing calls it yet. `RewriteError` is still `crate::const_rewrite::RewriteError` (Story 22 moves it here unchanged), so the constant parser is a private copy in this file until then. The code holds no landmine marker.

```rust
//! Access extraction: the query-to-views half of the per-query index build.
//!
//! A body atom such as `p(X, c42, X, Y)` is not a relation the executors can
//! descend as written: `c42` is a constant and `X` repeats. Relational
//! algebra reads it as a selection and a projection over `p`,
//! `π_{X,Y}(σ_{col1 = 42 ∧ col0 = col2}(p))`, and that is what an
//! [`Access`] records: the relation, a [`Filter`] (the selection) and the
//! kept columns (the projection) with the variable each one binds. The
//! build copies a relation through such a view once, so the executors see
//! only distinct variables and no constants.
//!
//! [`extract_accesses`] runs on the query after
//! [`crate::rewrite_placeholders`]. Each atom of the access query it returns
//! is named `@<k>` (see [`ACCESS_PREFIX`]) so the optimisers plan over
//! accesses; a name no relation can have, since the parser admits
//! `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only.

use {crate::const_rewrite::RewriteError, kermit_iters::Filter, kermit_parser::JoinQuery};

/// Prefix of the ids of the atoms of an [`AccessQuery`]: `@0`, `@1`, …, the
/// position of the access in [`AccessQuery::accesses`].
pub const ACCESS_PREFIX: &str = "@";

/// One body atom read as a selection and a projection of its relation.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Access {
    /// The relation the atom names.
    pub relation: String,
    /// The constants and column equalities the atom imposes on its rows.
    pub filter: Filter,
    /// The kept source columns, in source order: each variable's first
    /// occurrence in the atom.
    pub columns: Vec<usize>,
    /// The variable each kept column binds, parallel to `columns`.
    pub variables: Vec<String>,
}

/// A query's body as accesses.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct AccessQuery {
    /// The query with its head unchanged. `body[i]` is the atom `@{i}` over
    /// `accesses[i].variables`.
    pub query: JoinQuery,
    /// The body atoms with at least one kept column, in body order.
    pub accesses: Vec<Access>,
    /// The body atoms with none (only constants), in body order. Each is a
    /// test that some row matches, and its row count multiplies the answer.
    pub checks: Vec<Access>,
}

/// Reads every body atom of `query` as an [`Access`].
///
/// Expects [`crate::rewrite_placeholders`] to have run, and constants to be
/// `c<digits>`.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`RewriteError::BadAtom`] for the first constant, in body order,
/// that is not `c<digits>`.
///
/// # Panics
///
/// Panics if a body atom still holds a placeholder.
pub fn extract_accesses(query: &JoinQuery) -> Result<AccessQuery, RewriteError> {
    let _ = query;
    unimplemented!("replaced in Step 3")
}
```

```rust
pub fn extract_accesses(query: &JoinQuery) -> Result<AccessQuery, RewriteError> {
    let mut accesses: Vec<Access> = Vec::new();
    let mut checks: Vec<Access> = Vec::new();
    for atom in &query.body {
        let access = access_of(atom)?;
        if access.columns.is_empty() {
            checks.push(access);
        } else {
            accesses.push(access);
        }
    }
    let body = accesses
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(k, access)| Predicate {
            name: format!("{ACCESS_PREFIX}{k}"),
            terms: access.variables.iter().cloned().map(Term::Var).collect(),
        })
        .collect();
    Ok(AccessQuery {
        query: JoinQuery {
            head: query.head.clone(),
            body,
        },
        accesses,
        checks,
    })
}

/// One atom as an [`Access`], column by column.
fn access_of(atom: &Predicate) -> Result<Access, RewriteError> {
    let mut columns: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let mut variables: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let constants: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut equalities: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut first_column: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for (column, term) in atom.terms.iter().enumerate() {
        match term {
            | Term::Var(name) => match first_column.get(name.as_str()) {
                | Some(&first) => equalities.push((first, column)),
                | None => {
                    first_column.insert(name.as_str(), column);
                    columns.push(column);
                    variables.push(name.clone());
                },
            },
            | Term::Atom(_) => unimplemented!("constants: Task 9.2 replaces this arm"),
            | Term::Placeholder => panic!(
                "extract_accesses: placeholder in {atom}; run rewrite_placeholders first"
            ),
        }
    }
    Ok(Access {
        relation: atom.name.clone(),
        filter: Filter::new(constants, equalities),
        columns,
        variables,
    })
}
```

```rust
/// The dictionary id in a `c<digits>` constant.
fn parse_constant(text: &str) -> Result<usize, RewriteError> {
    let bad = || RewriteError::BadAtom(text.to_string());
    let digits = text.strip_prefix('c').ok_or_else(bad)?;
    if digits.is_empty() || !digits.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return Err(bad());
    }
    digits.parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| bad())
}
```

## Story 10: Index planning

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit-algos/src/index_plan.rs`, `kermit-algos/src/lib.rs`
- **Interfaces:** exposes `IndexSpec`, `IndexPlan`, `plan_indexes` and `INDEX_ID_PREFIX` to Stories 12 and 22; uses Story 9's `AccessQuery`, `analyse`, `canonical_names`, `QueryPlan`
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit-algos --lib index_plan`
- **Review:** deep

`plan_indexes` takes the access query and the plan an optimiser made for it, and decides what to build. Each access's kept columns are put in plan order (the order the plan binds their variables), which gives an `IndexSpec { relation, filter, columns }`. Identical specs merge, so a self-join that reads one relation one way builds it once, and the specs are numbered `#<k>` by first appearance. The executed query is rebuilt over those ids, each atom listing its variables in plan order, which is exactly the index's column order, so the executors need no reordering. The plan is translated by variable name, as `orient` does today, because `analyse` numbers body-only variables by first appearance and the rebuilt atoms can renumber them. `IndexSpec` has no header method (the names contract, "Index headers"): `RelationHeader` is a kermit-ds type, and Story 12 builds the header in `kermit::db`. Nothing calls this module yet; the old `orient` keeps serving the old pipeline until Story 22. The code holds no landmine marker.

```rust
//! Index planning: from a planned query of accesses to the indexes to build.
//!
//! The optimisers plan over the access query of [`crate::extract_accesses`],
//! one atom per access (`@0`, `@1`, …), and produce a variable order. The
//! executors descend every atom's columns in that order, so each access must
//! be read through a copy whose columns are already in it. [`plan_indexes`]
//! computes those copies: an access's kept columns sorted by the plan
//! position of the variable each binds, together with the access's filter,
//! is an [`IndexSpec`]. Two accesses with the same spec share one index.
//!
//! The query it returns names its atoms by index id (`#0`, `#1`, …, see
//! [`INDEX_ID_PREFIX`]), with each atom's variables in index column order,
//! so atom and index agree by construction and [`QueryPlan::validate`]
//! passes. It reads no data.

use {
    crate::{access::AccessQuery, optimiser::QueryPlan},
    kermit_iters::{Filter, TupleView, Tuples},
    kermit_parser::JoinQuery,
};

/// Prefix of the ids of the indexes in an executed query: `#0`, `#1`, …,
/// numbered by first appearance in the query. No relation name can collide
/// with it, since the parser admits `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only.
pub const INDEX_ID_PREFIX: &str = "#";

/// One index to build: a relation read through a filter, with the kept
/// source columns in plan order.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct IndexSpec {
    /// The relation the index is built from.
    pub relation: String,
    /// The constants and column equalities its rows satisfy.
    pub filter: Filter,
    /// The source columns it keeps, in plan order: column `i` of the index
    /// is column `columns[i]` of the relation.
    pub columns: Vec<usize>,
}

impl IndexSpec {
    /// This index as a view over `tuples`, the relation's flat rows.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if a column of the spec, or one its filter names, is not below
    /// `tuples.arity()` (see [`TupleView::new`]).
    pub fn view<'a>(&self, tuples: &'a Tuples) -> TupleView<'a> {
        TupleView::new(tuples, self.filter.clone(), self.columns.clone())
    }
}

/// A planned query, ready to build and execute.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct IndexPlan {
    /// The query to execute: the head unchanged, and `body[j]` the atom
    /// `#{id}` of the index the `j`-th access reads, over its variables in
    /// plan order.
    pub query: JoinQuery,
    /// The plan, translated to `query`'s variable numbering; it validates
    /// against `query`.
    pub plan: QueryPlan,
    /// The indexes to build, `indexes[id]`, with identical specs merged.
    pub indexes: Vec<IndexSpec>,
}

/// Plans the indexes of `accesses` under `plan`.
///
/// `plan` must have been made for `accesses.query`. Checks (the atoms with
/// no kept column) need no index and are not read here.
///
/// # Panics
///
/// Panics if `plan` is not a plan of `accesses.query`.
pub fn plan_indexes(accesses: &AccessQuery, plan: &QueryPlan) -> IndexPlan {
    let _ = (accesses, plan);
    unimplemented!("replaced in Step 3")
}

        let query: JoinQuery = text.parse().expect("parse");

    /// `order` (variable names) as a plan of `query`.
    fn plan_of(query: &JoinQuery, order: &[&str]) -> QueryPlan {
        let names = canonical_names(query);
        QueryPlan {
            variable_ordering: order
                .iter()
                .map(|name| names.iter().position(|n| n == name).expect("a query variable"))
                .collect(),
        }
    }

    fn planned(text: &str, order: &[&str]) -> IndexPlan {
        let accesses = accesses_of(text);
        let plan = plan_of(&accesses.query, order);
        plan_indexes(&accesses, &plan)
    }

    fn body_text(query: &JoinQuery) -> Vec<String> {
        query.body.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect()
    }

    fn spec(relation: &str, filter: Filter, columns: Vec<usize>) -> IndexSpec {
        IndexSpec {
            relation: relation.to_string(),
            filter,
            columns,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn view_reads_the_filtered_columns_in_spec_order() {
        let tuples = Tuples::from_flat(3, 3, vec![1, 2, 5, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 6]);
        let index = spec("r", Filter::new(vec![(2, 5)], vec![]), vec![1, 0]);
        let view = index.view(&tuples);
        let mut rows: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
        view.for_each(|row| rows.push(row.to_vec()));
        assert_eq!(rows, vec![vec![2, 1], vec![4, 3]]);
        assert_eq!(view.count(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn atoms_that_agree_with_the_plan_keep_their_column_order() {
        let out = planned("Q(X, Y, Z) :- R(X, Y), S(Y, Z), T(X, Z).", &["X", "Y", "Z"]);
        assert_eq!(out.indexes, vec![
            spec("R", Filter::none(), vec![0, 1]),
            spec("S", Filter::none(), vec![0, 1]),
            spec("T", Filter::none(), vec![0, 1]),
        ]);
        assert_eq!(body_text(&out.query), vec!["#0(X, Y)", "#1(Y, Z)", "#2(X, Z)"]);
        assert_eq!(out.plan.variable_ordering, vec![0, 1, 2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_reversed_order_reads_the_columns_reversed() {
        let out = planned("Q(X, Y) :- edge(Y, X).", &["X", "Y"]);
        assert_eq!(out.indexes, vec![spec("edge", Filter::none(), vec![1, 0])]);
        assert_eq!(body_text(&out.query), vec!["#0(X, Y)"]);
        assert_eq!(out.plan.variable_ordering, vec![0, 1]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_filter_is_carried_and_the_columns_are_source_columns() {
        // `r(X, c5, Y)` keeps columns 0 and 2; binding Y first reads them as (2, 0).
        let out = planned("Q(Y, X) :- r(X, c5, Y).", &["Y", "X"]);
        assert_eq!(out.indexes, vec![spec(
            "r",
            Filter::new(vec![(1, 5)], vec![]),
            vec![2, 0]
        )]);
        assert_eq!(body_text(&out.query), vec!["#0(Y, X)"]);

        // The equality names source columns, so it does not move with the order.
        let out = planned("Q(X, Y) :- r(Y, X, Y).", &["X", "Y"]);
        assert_eq!(out.indexes, vec![spec(
            "r",
            Filter::new(vec![], vec![(0, 2)]),
            vec![1, 0]
        )]);
        assert_eq!(body_text(&out.query), vec!["#0(X, Y)"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_head_is_unchanged() {
        let accesses = accesses_of("Q(Z, X) :- R(X, Y), S(Y, Z).");
        let plan = plan_of(&accesses.query, &["Z", "Y", "X"]);
        let out = plan_indexes(&accesses, &plan);
        assert_eq!(out.query.head, accesses.query.head);
    }

    #[test]
    fn checks_are_not_indexed() {
        let out = planned("Q(X) :- p(X), r(c1, c2).", &["X"]);
        assert_eq!(out.indexes, vec![spec("p", Filter::none(), vec![0])]);
        assert_eq!(body_text(&out.query), vec!["#0(X)"]);
    }

    /// A body of only constants has no access: `extract_accesses` returns an
    /// `AccessQuery` with no accesses, and `plan_indexes` must answer with no
    /// index, an empty body and the empty plan, not panic. The parser needs
    /// a head term, so the head is emptied to give the query no variable.
    #[test]
    fn a_query_with_no_accesses_plans_no_indexes() {
        let mut query: JoinQuery = "Q(c9) :- r(c1, c2), s(c3).".parse().expect("parse");
        query.head.terms.clear();
        let accesses = extract_accesses(&rewrite_placeholders(query)).expect("extract");
        assert!(accesses.accesses.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(accesses.checks.len(), 2);

        let plan = QueryPlan {
            variable_ordering: vec![],
        };
        let out = plan_indexes(&accesses, &plan);
        assert!(out.indexes.is_empty());
        assert!(out.query.body.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(out.query.head, accesses.query.head);
        assert!(out.plan.variable_ordering.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(out.plan.validate(&analyse(&out.query)), Ok(()));
    }

    /// `analyse` numbers body-only variables by first appearance, and the
    /// rebuilt atom lists them in plan order, so the numbers move; the plan
    /// follows the names, not the numbers.
    #[test]
    fn the_plan_is_translated_by_variable_name() {
        let accesses = accesses_of("Q(X) :- r(B, X, A).");
        // Numbering of the access query: X = 0, B = 1, A = 2.
        let old = plan_of(&accesses.query, &["X", "A", "B"]);
        assert_eq!(old.variable_ordering, vec![0, 2, 1]);

        let out = plan_indexes(&accesses, &old);
        assert_eq!(out.indexes, vec![spec("r", Filter::none(), vec![1, 2, 0])]);
        assert_eq!(body_text(&out.query), vec!["#0(X, A, B)"]);
        // Numbering of the executed query: X = 0, A = 1, B = 2.
        assert_eq!(out.plan.variable_ordering, vec![0, 1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(out.plan.validate(&analyse(&out.query)), Ok(()));
        // The untranslated plan would not have validated.
        assert!(old.validate(&analyse(&out.query)).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_order_of_the_triangle_yields_a_valid_plan_with_the_same_order() {
        let orders: [[&str; 3]; 6] = [
            ["X", "Y", "Z"],
            ["X", "Z", "Y"],
            ["Y", "X", "Z"],
            ["Y", "Z", "X"],
            ["Z", "X", "Y"],
            ["Z", "Y", "X"],
        ];
        for order in orders {
            let out = planned("Q(X, Y, Z) :- R(X, Y), S(Y, Z), T(X, Z).", &order);
            assert_eq!(out.plan.validate(&analyse(&out.query)), Ok(()), "{order:?}");
            let names = canonical_names(&out.query);
            let bound: Vec<&str> = out
                .plan
                .variable_ordering
                .iter()
                .map(|&v| names[v].as_str())
                .collect();
            assert_eq!(bound, order.to_vec());
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
pub fn plan_indexes(accesses: &AccessQuery, plan: &QueryPlan) -> IndexPlan {
    let source = &accesses.query;
    let names = canonical_names(source);
    let plan_names: Vec<&str> = plan
        .variable_ordering
        .iter()
        .map(|&v| names[v].as_str())
        .collect();
    let position: HashMap<&str, usize> = plan_names
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(at, &name)| (name, at))
        .collect();

    let mut indexes: Vec<IndexSpec> = Vec::new();
    let mut body: Vec<Predicate> = Vec::with_capacity(accesses.accesses.len());
    for access in &accesses.accesses {
        // `order[j]` is the kept column that goes `j`-th: the kept columns
        // sorted by the plan position of the variable each binds. A
        // variable occurs once per access, so the positions are distinct.
        let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..access.columns.len()).collect();
        order.sort_by_key(|&kept| position[access.variables[kept].as_str()]);
        let spec = IndexSpec {
            relation: access.relation.clone(),
            filter: access.filter.clone(),
            columns: order.iter().map(|&kept| access.columns[kept]).collect(),
        };
        let id = indexes.len();
        indexes.push(spec);
        body.push(Predicate {
            name: format!("{INDEX_ID_PREFIX}{id}"),
            terms: order
                .iter()
                .map(|&kept| Term::Var(access.variables[kept].clone()))
                .collect(),
        });
    }
    let query = JoinQuery {
        head: source.head.clone(),
        body,
    };

    // `analyse` numbers body-only variables by first appearance, and the
    // atoms above list their variables in plan order, so the numbers can
    // move: translate the plan by name.
    let renumbered = canonical_names(&query);
    let index_of: HashMap<&str, usize> = renumbered
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(at, name)| (name.as_str(), at))
        .collect();
    let plan = QueryPlan {
        variable_ordering: plan_names.iter().map(|name| index_of[name]).collect(),
    };
    debug_assert_eq!(
        plan.validate(&analyse(&query)),
        Ok(()),
        "every atom lists its variables in plan order"
    );

    IndexPlan {
        query,
        plan,
        indexes,
    }
}
```

## Story 11: The catalog

- **Developer:** junior-dev
- **Files:** `kermit/src/db/catalog.rs`, `kermit/src/db.rs`
- **Interfaces:** exposes `Catalog` to Stories 12–20; uses `RelationStats`, `StatisticsLevel`, `distinct_per_column`, `RelationArities`
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit --lib db::catalog`
- **Review:** light (a new type over existing statistics helpers, no landmine)

`Catalog` holds each relation's header and flat `Tuples`, keyed by header name, and nothing
else: no structure is built over it. It gathers statistics once when it is created: row counts
always, and column-distinct counts at `StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct` through
`distinct_per_column` over the flat rows. A later relation with the same name replaces an
earlier one, as `Database`'s map does today. It implements `RelationArities`, so
`validate_query` can read it (Story 20 changes that function's signature; this story does not
touch it). Nothing calls `Catalog` yet: it is `pub`, so there is no dead-code warning, and
Story 12 is its first user. The unit tests cover lookups, the statistics at both levels, row
counts that count duplicate rows, a duplicate name replacing the earlier relation, and the
arities. No code in this story holds a landmine marker.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// `edge/2` with named attributes: four rows, three distinct values in
    /// each column.
    fn edge() -> (RelationHeader, Tuples) {
        (
            RelationHeader::new("edge", vec!["src".into(), "dst".into()]),
            Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 10], vec![1, 20], vec![2, 10], vec![3, 30]]),
        )
    }

    /// `r/3` with positional attributes: two rows.
    fn r() -> (RelationHeader, Tuples) {
        (
            RelationHeader::new_positional("r", 3),
            Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2, 3], vec![1, 2, 4]]),
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn relations_are_found_by_header_name() {
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![r(), edge()], StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts);
        assert_eq!(catalog.header("edge").unwrap().attrs(), ["src", "dst"]);
        assert_eq!(catalog.tuples("edge").unwrap().len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(catalog.tuples("r").unwrap().arity(), 3);
        assert!(catalog.header("nope").is_none());
        assert!(catalog.tuples("nope").is_none());
        assert!(catalog.statistics("nope").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_come_back_sorted_whatever_the_input_order() {
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![r(), edge()], StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts);
        assert_eq!(catalog.names().collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["edge", "r"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tuple_counts_hold_row_counts_and_no_column_counts() {
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![edge(), r()], StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts);
        assert_eq!(catalog.level(), StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts);
        assert_eq!(catalog.statistics("edge"), Some(&RelationStats::new(4, 2)));
        assert_eq!(catalog.statistics("r"), Some(&RelationStats::new(2, 3)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn column_distinct_counts_each_column() {
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![edge(), r()], StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct);
        assert_eq!(catalog.level(), StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct);
        assert_eq!(
            catalog.statistics("edge"),
            Some(&RelationStats::new(4, 2).with_column_distinct(vec![3, 3]))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            catalog.statistics("r"),
            Some(&RelationStats::new(2, 3).with_column_distinct(vec![1, 1, 2]))
        );
    }

    /// The catalog is flat: a repeated row is a row, so it adds to the row
    /// count and not to any column's distinct count.
    #[test]
    fn a_repeated_row_counts_as_a_row_but_not_as_a_distinct_value() {
        let (header, mut tuples) = edge();
        tuples.push(&[1, 10]);
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![(header, tuples)], StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct);
        assert_eq!(
            catalog.statistics("edge"),
            Some(&RelationStats::new(5, 2).with_column_distinct(vec![3, 3]))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_relation_has_zero_counts() {
        let empty = (RelationHeader::new_positional("e", 2), Tuples::new(2));
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![empty], StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct);
        assert_eq!(
            catalog.statistics("e"),
            Some(&RelationStats::new(0, 2).with_column_distinct(vec![0, 0]))
        );
    }

    /// As `Database`'s map does, the last relation with a name wins, with
    /// its own header, tuples and statistics.
    #[test]
    fn a_later_duplicate_name_replaces_the_earlier_relation() {
        let later = (
            RelationHeader::new_positional("edge", 3),
            Tuples::from(vec![vec![7, 8, 9]]),
        );
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![edge(), later], StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct);
        assert_eq!(catalog.names().count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(catalog.header("edge").unwrap().arity(), 3);
        assert_eq!(catalog.tuples("edge").unwrap().to_vecs(), vec![vec![7, 8, 9]]);
        assert_eq!(
            catalog.statistics("edge"),
            Some(&RelationStats::new(1, 3).with_column_distinct(vec![1, 1, 1]))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn arities_and_names_are_those_of_the_headers() {
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![r(), edge()], StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts);
        assert_eq!(catalog.arity("edge"), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(catalog.arity("r"), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(catalog.arity("nope"), None);
        assert_eq!(catalog.relation_names(), vec!["edge".to_string(), "r".to_string()]);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The flat relation store a query is prepared and built from.

use {
    super::RelationArities,
    kermit_algos::{distinct_per_column, RelationStats, StatisticsLevel},
    kermit_ds::{RelationHeader, Tuples},
    std::collections::BTreeMap,
};

/// One relation: its header, its rows, and the statistics gathered from
/// them when the catalog was created.
struct Entry {
    header: RelationHeader,
    tuples: Tuples,
    statistics: RelationStats,
}

/// Relations by name, each as a header and one flat [`Tuples`] batch, plus
/// the statistics a query optimiser reads.
///
/// A catalog is the untimed side of a query's life: relations are loaded
/// into it once, and every query then builds the indexes it needs from
/// these rows ([`TupleView`](kermit_iters::TupleView)s over them) and
/// times only that build. It holds no data structure, so the cost of
/// loading does not depend on which structure a query later builds.
///
/// The statistics are gathered once, in [`new`](Self::new), up to the
/// [`StatisticsLevel`] asked for, and cannot change afterwards, so they
/// cannot drift from the rows. Create it at the level the optimiser
/// declares ([`Planner::required_statistics`]); a planner that asks for
/// more than the catalog holds is rejected by `prepare` with
/// [`JoinError::MissingStatistics`](super::JoinError::MissingStatistics).
///
/// [`Planner::required_statistics`]: kermit_algos::Planner::required_statistics
pub struct Catalog {
    relations: BTreeMap<String, Entry>,
    level: StatisticsLevel,
}

impl Catalog {
    /// Creates a catalog over `relations`, keyed by each header's
    /// [`name`](RelationHeader::name). A later relation with the same name
    /// replaces an earlier one.
    ///
    /// Tuple counts are the row counts of the batches, so they cost
    /// nothing. [`StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct`] also walks each
    /// relation's rows once to count each column's distinct values:
    /// O(N · arity) time, O(distinct values) space.
    pub fn new(relations: Vec<(RelationHeader, Tuples)>, level: StatisticsLevel) -> Catalog {
        let mut held: BTreeMap<String, (RelationHeader, Tuples)> = BTreeMap::new();
        for (header, tuples) in relations {
            held.insert(header.name().to_string(), (header, tuples));
        }
        // Statistics are gathered after the names are settled, so a relation
        // that a later duplicate replaced is never walked.
        let relations = held
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(name, (header, tuples))| {
                let arity = header.arity();
                let mut statistics = RelationStats::new(tuples.len(), arity);
                if level >= StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct {
                    let column_distinct = distinct_per_column(arity, |visit| {
                        for row in tuples.rows() {
                            visit(row);
                        }
                    });
                    statistics = statistics.with_column_distinct(column_distinct);
                }
                let entry = Entry {
                    header,
                    tuples,
                    statistics,
                };
                (name, entry)
            })
            .collect();
        Catalog { relations, level }
    }

    /// The header of the relation called `name`, if the catalog holds one.
    pub fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&RelationHeader> {
        self.relations.get(name).map(|entry| &entry.header)
    }

    /// The rows of the relation called `name`, if the catalog holds one.
    pub fn tuples(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Tuples> {
        self.relations.get(name).map(|entry| &entry.tuples)
    }

    /// The statistics gathered for `name`, if the catalog holds it.
    pub fn statistics(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&RelationStats> {
        self.relations.get(name).map(|entry| &entry.statistics)
    }

    /// How far the statistics go.
    pub fn level(&self) -> StatisticsLevel { self.level }

    /// Every relation name, in name order.
    pub fn names(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        self.relations.keys().map(String::as_str)
    }
}

impl RelationArities for Catalog {
    fn arity(&self, relation: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.header(relation).map(RelationHeader::arity)
    }

    fn relation_names(&self) -> Vec<String> { self.names().map(str::to_string).collect() }
}
```

## Story 12: Prepare, build and execute

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit/src/db/lifecycle.rs`, `kermit/src/db.rs`, `kermit-algos/src/optimiser/planner.rs`
- **Interfaces:** exposes `Prepared`, `prepare`, `Indexes`, `build_with`, `build` and `execute` to Stories 13–20; uses Stories 2, 9, 10 and 11
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit --lib db::lifecycle`
- **Review:** deep

`kermit/src/db/lifecycle.rs` is the new pipeline's three steps over a `Catalog`, written beside the old `Database` pipeline, which it does not touch. `prepare` (untimed) validates the query with `validate_query` under `ColumnOrderPolicy::Any`, rewrites `_`, extracts the accesses, refuses a planner that reads more statistics than the catalog holds, takes each access's statistics (an unfiltered access reads its relation's catalog entry; a filtered one is counted, and its columns' distinct values are counted when the optimiser asks, by scanning the flat tuples through its view), plans the query of accesses and calls `plan_indexes`. It also counts each index view's rows once, so the timed build does not scan a filtered relation a second time only to report `Indexes::rows()`. `build_with` (timed) turns each spec into a view and hands it, with the header `spec_header` makes (the amended contract: `IndexSpec` has no `header` method), to the constructor, and counts each constant check into the multiplicity (clamped to 1 unless `R::KEEPS_DUPLICATES`). `execute` (timed) runs `JoinAlgo::join_for_each` over the indexes, emits each row's head prefix once per unit of multiplicity, and, when every atom was a check, emits the empty head row `multiplicity` times without joining. The work is three tasks, each leaving the tree green: `Prepared` and `prepare`, then `Indexes`, `build_with` and `build`, then `execute`. Until Story 23 retires the column-order policy, `prepare` builds its statistics under `ColumnOrderPolicy::Any` whatever policy the `Planner` it receives was made with, so Task 12.1 also deletes `Planner::plan`'s `debug_assert_eq!` that the statistics match the planner's policy (and the doc sentence requiring it) in `kermit-algos/src/optimiser/planner.rs`: `plan` then just calls the optimiser, and a `Planner::stored` planner prepares freely. The old pipeline still builds its statistics under the planner's policy, so its behaviour is unchanged. The code holds no landmine marker.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use {
        super::*,
        kermit_algos::{analyse, LexicographicOptimiser, QueryOptimiser, RewriteError},
        kermit_ds::{Filter, RelationHeader},
        std::{cell::RefCell, rc::Rc},
    };

    /// A catalog of positional relations, each `(name, arity, rows)`, gathered at `level`.
    fn catalog_at(
        level: StatisticsLevel, relations: Vec<(&str, usize, Vec<Vec<usize>>)>,
    ) -> Catalog {
        let relations = relations
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(name, arity, rows)| {
                let mut tuples = Tuples::new(arity);
                for row in &rows {
                    tuples.push(row);
                }
                (RelationHeader::new_positional(name, arity), tuples)
            })
            .collect();
        Catalog::new(relations, level)
    }

    /// [`catalog_at`] at tuple counts, which is all the default optimiser reads.
    fn catalog(relations: Vec<(&str, usize, Vec<Vec<usize>>)>) -> Catalog {
        catalog_at(StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts, relations)
    }

    fn parse(text: &str) -> JoinQuery { text.parse().expect("a well-formed query") }

    /// A planner for `optimiser` under the only policy `prepare` plans with.
    fn planner_of(optimiser: impl QueryOptimiser + 'static) -> Planner {
        Planner::new(Box::new(optimiser), ColumnOrderPolicy::Any)
    }

    /// Plans in canonical variable order, so a test can read the plan off the query.
    fn lexicographic() -> Planner { planner_of(LexicographicOptimiser) }

    fn prepared_for(catalog: &Catalog, text: &str) -> Prepared {
        prepare(catalog, &parse(text), &lexicographic()).expect("a valid query")
    }

    fn spec(relation: &str, filter: Filter, columns: Vec<usize>) -> IndexSpec {
        IndexSpec {
            relation: relation.into(),
            filter,
            columns,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_constant_filters_the_index() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("p", 2, vec![vec![1, 10], vec![2, 20], vec![3, 30]])]);
        let prepared = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X) :- p(X, c10).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec(
            "p",
            Filter::new(vec![(1, 10)], vec![]),
            vec![0]
        )]);
        assert!(prepared.checks().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(prepared.relations(), vec!["p"]);
        assert_eq!(prepared.head_len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(prepared.query().to_string(), "Q(X) :- #0(X).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.plan().variable_ordering, vec![0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_repeated_variable_becomes_an_equality() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("r", 2, vec![vec![1, 1], vec![1, 2], vec![2, 3], vec![3, 3]])]);
        let prepared = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X, X).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec(
            "r",
            Filter::new(vec![], vec![(0, 1)]),
            vec![0]
        )]);
        assert_eq!(prepared.query().to_string(), "Q(X) :- #0(X).");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_constant_and_a_repeat_share_one_filter() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("t", 3, vec![vec![1, 5, 1], vec![1, 5, 2], vec![2, 6, 2]])]);
        let prepared = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X) :- t(X, c5, X).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec(
            "t",
            Filter::new(vec![(1, 5)], vec![(0, 2)]),
            vec![0]
        )]);
    }

    /// `r(X, X)` is a filtered read of `r` and `r(X, Y)` an unfiltered one: two indexes.
    #[test]
    fn mixed_occurrences_of_one_relation_get_two_indexes() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("r", 2, vec![vec![1, 1], vec![1, 2], vec![2, 3], vec![3, 3]])]);
        let prepared = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X, Y) :- r(X, X), r(X, Y).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.indexes().to_vec(), vec![
            spec("r", Filter::new(vec![], vec![(0, 1)]), vec![0]),
            spec("r", Filter::none(), vec![0, 1]),
        ]);
        assert_eq!(prepared.query().to_string(), "Q(X, Y) :- #0(X), #1(X, Y).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.relations(), vec!["r"]);
    }

    /// A `_` is an unused named variable, so its column is kept. In the middle the plan binds
    /// `Z` before the placeholder's variable, so the index reads columns 0, 2, 1.
    #[test]
    fn a_placeholder_is_a_kept_column() {
        let c = catalog(vec![
            ("r", 2, vec![vec![1, 2]]),
            ("t", 3, vec![vec![1, 2, 3]]),
        ]);
        let trailing = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X, _).");
        assert_eq!(trailing.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec("r", Filter::none(), vec![0, 1])]);
        let middle = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X, Z) :- t(X, _, Z).");
        assert_eq!(middle.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec("t", Filter::none(), vec![0, 2, 1])]);
        assert_eq!(middle.head_len(), 2);
    }

    /// Three reads of `e`, all in the same column order: one index, read three times.
    #[test]
    fn a_self_join_reads_one_merged_index() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("e", 2, vec![vec![1, 2], vec![2, 3], vec![1, 3]])]);
        let prepared = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X, Y, Z) :- e(X, Y), e(Y, Z), e(X, Z).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec("e", Filter::none(), vec![0, 1])]);
        assert_eq!(
            prepared.query().to_string(),
            "Q(X, Y, Z) :- #0(X, Y), #0(Y, Z), #0(X, Z)."
        );
        assert_eq!(prepared.relations(), vec!["e"]);
        assert_eq!(prepared.plan().validate(&analyse(prepared.query())), Ok(()));
    }

    /// Reading a relation against its stored column order needs no copy protocol: the index
    /// is simply built reversed, and `edge(X, Y), edge(Y, X)` gets two.
    #[test]
    fn a_reversed_atom_gets_its_own_index() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("edge", 2, vec![vec![1, 2], vec![3, 4]])]);
        let reversed = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X, Y) :- edge(Y, X).");
        assert_eq!(reversed.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec("edge", Filter::none(), vec![1, 0])]);
        assert_eq!(reversed.query().to_string(), "Q(X, Y) :- #0(X, Y).");

        let cycle = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X, Y) :- edge(X, Y), edge(Y, X).");
        assert_eq!(cycle.indexes().to_vec(), vec![
            spec("edge", Filter::none(), vec![0, 1]),
            spec("edge", Filter::none(), vec![1, 0]),
        ]);
        assert_eq!(cycle.query().to_string(), "Q(X, Y) :- #0(X, Y), #1(X, Y).");
    }

    /// An atom with no variable needs no index: it is a check, and its relation is still read.
    #[test]
    fn all_constant_atoms_become_checks() {
        let c = catalog(vec![
            ("r", 1, vec![vec![1], vec![2]]),
            ("s", 2, vec![vec![7, 8], vec![9, 9]]),
        ]);
        let prepared = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X), s(c7, c8).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.indexes().to_vec(), vec![spec("r", Filter::none(), vec![0])]);
        assert_eq!(prepared.checks().to_vec(), vec![Access {
            relation: "s".into(),
            filter: Filter::new(vec![(0, 7), (1, 8)], vec![]),
            columns: vec![],
            variables: vec![],
        }]);
        assert_eq!(prepared.relations(), vec!["r", "s"]);
        assert_eq!(prepared.query().to_string(), "Q(X) :- #0(X).");
        assert_eq!(prepared.head_len(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_malformed_query_is_refused_with_validations_error() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("edge", 2, vec![vec![1, 2]])]);
        let refused = |text: &str| prepare(&c, &parse(text), &lexicographic()).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(refused("Q(X) :- missing(X)."), JoinError::UnknownRelation {
            relation: "missing".into(),
            known: vec!["edge".into()],
        });
        assert_eq!(refused("Q(X) :- edge(X)."), JoinError::ArityMismatch {
            atom: "edge(X)".into(),
            relation: "edge".into(),
            terms: 1,
            arity: 2,
        });
        assert_eq!(
            refused("Q(X) :- edge(X, cfoo)."),
            JoinError::MalformedConstant(RewriteError::BadAtom("cfoo".into()))
        );
        assert_eq!(refused("Q(Z) :- edge(X, Y)."), JoinError::UnboundHeadVariable {
            variable: "Z".into(),
        });
    }

    /// Plans like `lexicographic` but declares that it reads per-column distinct counts.
    struct NeedsColumns;

    impl QueryOptimiser for NeedsColumns {
        fn plan(&self, query: &JoinQuery, stats: &CatalogStats) -> QueryPlan {
            LexicographicOptimiser.plan(query, stats)
        }

        fn required_statistics(&self) -> StatisticsLevel { StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct }
    }

    /// A query that fails validation reports that error, not `MissingStatistics`: the
    /// statistics check runs after validation.
    #[test]
    fn validation_errors_win_over_missing_statistics() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("edge", 2, vec![vec![1, 2]])]);
        let refused = prepare(&c, &parse("Q(X) :- missing(X)."), &planner_of(NeedsColumns));
        assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), JoinError::UnknownRelation {
            relation: "missing".into(),
            known: vec!["edge".into()],
        });
    }

    /// An optimiser that reads more than the catalog gathered is refused, and the same
    /// relations gathered at its level are prepared.
    #[test]
    fn an_optimiser_reading_ungathered_statistics_is_refused() {
        let relations = || {
            vec![
                ("first", 1, vec![vec![1], vec![2], vec![3]]),
                ("second", 1, vec![vec![2], vec![3], vec![4]]),
            ]
        };
        let query = parse("Q(X) :- first(X), second(X).");
        let planner = planner_of(NeedsColumns);
        let refused = prepare(&catalog(relations()), &query, &planner);
        assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), JoinError::MissingStatistics {
            required: StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct,
            available: StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts,
        });
        let analysed = catalog_at(StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct, relations());
        assert!(prepare(&analysed, &query, &planner).is_ok());
    }

    /// Plans like `lexicographic`, records the query and statistics it is handed, and declares
    /// that it reads `level`. Clones share the record, so a test keeps one while the planner
    /// owns the other.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct StatsSpy {
        level: StatisticsLevel,
        seen: Rc<RefCell<Option<(JoinQuery, CatalogStats)>>>,
    }

    impl StatsSpy {
        fn new(level: StatisticsLevel) -> Self {
            StatsSpy {
                level,
                seen: Rc::default(),
            }
        }

        /// What the optimiser was handed by the last `prepare`.
        fn taken(&self) -> (JoinQuery, CatalogStats) {
            self.seen.borrow_mut().take().expect("the optimiser planned")
        }
    }

    impl QueryOptimiser for StatsSpy {
        fn plan(&self, query: &JoinQuery, stats: &CatalogStats) -> QueryPlan {
            *self.seen.borrow_mut() = Some((query.clone(), stats.clone()));
            LexicographicOptimiser.plan(query, stats)
        }

        fn required_statistics(&self) -> StatisticsLevel { self.level }
    }

    /// Three relations for [`STATISTICS_QUERY`]. `r` has two diagonal rows, `s` has three rows
    /// with 5 in its second column, and `u` is read whole.
    fn statistics_relations() -> Vec<(&'static str, usize, Vec<Vec<usize>>)> {
        vec![
            ("r", 2, vec![vec![1, 1], vec![1, 2], vec![2, 3], vec![3, 3]]),
            ("s", 3, vec![
                vec![1, 5, 7],
                vec![1, 5, 8],
                vec![3, 5, 9],
                vec![3, 6, 7],
                vec![4, 6, 6],
            ]),
            ("u", 2, vec![vec![1, 2], vec![1, 3], vec![2, 3], vec![2, 4]]),
        ]
    }

    const STATISTICS_QUERY: &str = "Q(X, Y) :- r(X, X), s(X, c5, W), u(X, Y).";

    /// The planner plans the query of accesses and reads statistics keyed by access id: a
    /// filtered access is counted through its filter, an unfiltered one is its relation's.
    #[test]
    fn the_planner_reads_statistics_of_the_accesses() {
        let c = catalog_at(StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct, statistics_relations());
        let spy = StatsSpy::new(StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct);
        prepare(&c, &parse(STATISTICS_QUERY), &planner_of(spy.clone())).unwrap();
        let (planned, stats) = spy.taken();

        assert_eq!(planned.to_string(), "Q(X, Y) :- @0(X), @1(X, W), @2(X, Y).");
        // r(X, X): the rows (1, 1) and (3, 3), kept column 0.
        assert_eq!(stats.tuples("@0"), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(stats.distinct("@0", 0), Some(2));
        // s(X, c5, W): the rows (1, 5, 7), (1, 5, 8) and (3, 5, 9), kept columns 0 and 2.
        assert_eq!(stats.tuples("@1"), Some(3));
        assert_eq!((stats.distinct("@1", 0), stats.distinct("@1", 1)), (Some(2), Some(3)));
        // u(X, Y): unfiltered, so the catalog's own statistics.
        assert_eq!(stats.tuples("@2"), Some(4));
        assert_eq!((stats.distinct("@2", 0), stats.distinct("@2", 1)), (Some(2), Some(3)));
        // Nothing is keyed by the relations' own names.
        assert_eq!(stats.tuples("r"), None);
    }

    /// An optimiser that reads only tuple counts gets exact counts of the filtered accesses
    /// and no distinct counts, so no filtered scan pays for what nobody reads.
    #[test]
    fn a_planner_reading_only_counts_gets_counts_of_filtered_accesses() {
        let c = catalog(statistics_relations());
        let spy = StatsSpy::new(StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts);
        prepare(&c, &parse(STATISTICS_QUERY), &planner_of(spy.clone())).unwrap();
        let (_, stats) = spy.taken();
        let counts = (stats.tuples("@0"), stats.tuples("@1"), stats.tuples("@2"));
        assert_eq!(counts, (Some(2), Some(3), Some(4)));
        for id in ["@0", "@1", "@2"] {
            assert_eq!(stats.distinct(id, 0), None, "{id}");
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! One query over a [`Catalog`], in three steps. `prepare` runs once and is not timed: it
//! validates the query, gives each body atom an access, plans over the accesses and decides
//! which indexes the plan reads. `build` and `execute` are what a benchmark times: `build`
//! copies each index out of the catalog's flat tuples, and `execute` joins them.

use {
    super::{validate_query, Catalog, JoinError},
    kermit_algos::{
        distinct_per_column, extract_accesses, plan_indexes, rewrite_placeholders, Access,
        CatalogStats, ColumnOrderPolicy, IndexPlan, IndexSpec, JoinQuery, Planner, QueryPlan,
        RelationStats, StatisticsLevel, ACCESS_PREFIX,
    },
    kermit_ds::{TupleView, Tuples},
    std::collections::BTreeMap,
};

/// What a [`Prepared`] expects of the catalog it is used with: `prepare` checked it, so a
/// missing relation means another catalog was passed.
const CATALOG_HOLDS: &str =
    "`prepare` checked that the catalog holds every relation the query reads";

/// A query planned over a [`Catalog`]: what [`prepare`] decides, and all that building and
/// executing need besides the catalog itself.
///
/// It holds the executed query (the head as written, and one atom per body atom that binds a
/// variable, named `#0`, `#1`, … after the index it reads, over its variables in plan order),
/// the plan for that query, the index specs, and the constant checks (the atoms with no
/// variable, which only count rows). It borrows nothing, and is meant for the catalog it was
/// prepared over.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Prepared {
    query: JoinQuery,
    plan: QueryPlan,
    indexes: Vec<IndexSpec>,
    checks: Vec<Access>,
    head_len: usize,
}

impl Prepared {
    /// The executed query: the head as written, and one atom `#<id>` per body atom that binds
    /// a variable.
    pub fn query(&self) -> &JoinQuery { &self.query }

    /// The plan for [`query`](Self::query); it validates against it.
    pub fn plan(&self) -> &QueryPlan { &self.plan }

    /// The indexes the query reads, `indexes()[id]` being `#<id>`. Identical specs are merged,
    /// so an atom list that reads one relation one way builds it once.
    pub fn indexes(&self) -> &[IndexSpec] { &self.indexes }

    /// The atoms with no variable, in body order. Each only has to count the rows its
    /// constants admit.
    pub fn checks(&self) -> &[Access] { &self.checks }

    /// The number of head terms: the length of the prefix of each joined row that `execute`
    /// lends to its sink.
    pub fn head_len(&self) -> usize { self.head_len }

    /// The distinct relations the query reads: those of its indexes in id order, then those of
    /// its checks, each at its first appearance.
    pub fn relations(&self) -> Vec<&str> {
        let mut names: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
        let read = self
            .indexes
            .iter()
            .map(|spec| spec.relation.as_str())
            .chain(self.checks.iter().map(|check| check.relation.as_str()));
        for name in read {
            if !names.contains(&name) {
                names.push(name);
            }
        }
        names
    }
}

/// Validates `query` against `catalog` and plans it: the untimed part of running a query.
///
/// The steps, in order: [`validate_query`]; rewrite each `_` into a fresh variable; extract
/// one access per body atom; refuse a planner that reads more statistics than the catalog
/// gathered; take each access's statistics (an unfiltered access is its relation's, a filtered
/// one is counted by scanning the relation through its filter); plan the query of accesses;
/// and turn that plan into index specs.
///
/// An index is built in plan order, so no stored column order constrains the plan: the
/// statistics are always built under [`ColumnOrderPolicy::Any`], whatever policy `planner` was
/// made with, and `planner` plans over them freely.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// The [`JoinError`] [`validate_query`] would return, or [`JoinError::MissingStatistics`]
/// when `planner` reads statistics the catalog does not hold; in both cases nothing has been
/// planned.
pub fn prepare(
    catalog: &Catalog, query: &JoinQuery, planner: &Planner,
) -> Result<Prepared, JoinError> {
    // The policy argument goes when `ColumnOrderPolicy` does.
    validate_query(query, catalog, ColumnOrderPolicy::Any)?;

    let rewritten = rewrite_placeholders(query.clone());
    let access_query = extract_accesses(&rewritten)?;

    // The plan comes from the catalog's statistics, so the optimiser must not read more than
    // the catalog gathered when it was built.
    let required = planner.required_statistics();
    if required > catalog.level() {
        return Err(JoinError::MissingStatistics {
            required,
            available: catalog.level(),
        });
    }

    let access_stats: BTreeMap<String, RelationStats> = access_query
        .accesses
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(k, access)| {
            let id = format!("{ACCESS_PREFIX}{k}");
            (id, access_statistics(catalog, access, required))
        })
        .collect();
    let stats = CatalogStats::for_query(&access_query.query, ColumnOrderPolicy::Any, |id| {
        access_stats.get(id).cloned()
    });
    let ordering = planner.plan(&access_query.query, &stats);

    let IndexPlan {
        query: executed,
        plan,
        indexes,
    } = plan_indexes(&access_query, &ordering);
    Ok(Prepared {
        query: executed,
        plan,
        indexes,
        checks: access_query.checks,
        head_len: query.head.terms.len(),
    })
}

/// The rows of `relation` in `catalog`.
fn tuples_of<'c>(catalog: &'c Catalog, relation: &str) -> &'c Tuples {
    catalog.tuples(relation).expect(CATALOG_HOLDS)
}

/// The statistics the planner reads for `access`. An access that keeps every row and column is
/// its relation's catalog entry. Any other is scanned through its view: the rows it admits,
/// and, when `level` asks for them, the distinct values in each column it keeps.
fn access_statistics(catalog: &Catalog, access: &Access, level: StatisticsLevel) -> RelationStats {
    let tuples = tuples_of(catalog, &access.relation);
    let view = TupleView::new(tuples, access.filter.clone(), access.columns.clone());
    if view.is_identity() {
        return catalog.statistics(&access.relation).expect(CATALOG_HOLDS).clone();
    }
    let stats = RelationStats::new(view.count(), view.arity());
    if level < StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct {
        return stats;
    }
    stats.with_column_distinct(distinct_per_column(view.arity(), |visit| view.for_each(visit)))
}
```

```rust
/// The header of `spec`'s index: named for the relation, with the attributes of `base` at the
/// spec's columns, or positional (at the index's arity) when `base` is.
fn spec_header(spec: &IndexSpec, base: &RelationHeader) -> RelationHeader {
    if base.attrs().is_empty() {
        RelationHeader::new_positional(&spec.relation, spec.columns.len())
    } else {
        let attrs = spec
            .columns
            .iter()
            .map(|&column| base.attrs()[column].clone())
            .collect();
        RelationHeader::new(&spec.relation, attrs)
    }
}

/// The indexes of one prepared query, made by [`build`] or [`build_with`]: one structure per
/// [`IndexSpec`], in id order, and what the constant checks decided.
///
/// The indexes hold copies of their rows and borrow nothing from the catalog, so a benchmark
/// can drop them after its timers stop.
pub struct Indexes<R> {
    /// The specs the indexes were built from, in id order.
    specs: Vec<IndexSpec>,
    /// `relations[id]` is index `#<id>`.
    relations: Vec<R>,
    multiplicity: usize,
    rows: usize,
}

impl<R> Indexes<R> {
    /// The index named `id` (`#0`, `#1`, …), if there is one. Only the exact spelling names
    /// an index.
    pub fn get(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&R> {
        let digits = id.strip_prefix(INDEX_ID_PREFIX)?;
        // `parse` alone would also take `#01` and `#+1`, which no id is spelled as.
        let padded = digits.len() > 1 && digits.starts_with('0');
        if padded || !digits.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {
            return None;
        }
        self.relations.get(digits.parse::<usize>().ok()?)
    }

    /// Each index with the spec it was built from, in id order.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&IndexSpec, &R)> {
        self.specs.iter().zip(&self.relations)
    }

    /// How many times `execute` emits each answer: the product of the constant checks'
    /// counts, each clamped to 1 unless the structure keeps duplicates
    /// ([`Relation::KEEPS_DUPLICATES`]). Zero when a check admits no row.
    pub fn multiplicity(&self) -> usize { self.multiplicity }

    /// The rows the build copied: the sum of the index views' counts, taken when the query was
    /// prepared.
    pub fn rows(&self) -> usize { self.rows }
}

/// Builds the indexes of `prepared` from `catalog`, constructing each with `construct`: the
/// timed build.
///
/// Each spec becomes a [`TupleView`] over its relation's flat tuples, handed with the index's
/// header to `construct` (normally [`Relation::from_view`], as [`build`] does; the binary's
/// families pass their own to carry a config and a build mode). Each constant check counts the
/// rows its constants admit, and the counts multiply into
/// [`multiplicity`](Indexes::multiplicity).
///
/// # Panics
///
/// If `prepared` was made over another catalog and a relation it reads is missing. In debug
/// builds, also if the catalog's rows changed since `prepare` counted them.
pub fn build_with<R: Relation>(
    catalog: &Catalog, prepared: &Prepared,
    mut construct: impl FnMut(RelationHeader, TupleView<'_>) -> R,
) -> Indexes<R> {
    // A check keeps no column: it only counts the rows its filter admits. A structure that
    // keeps duplicates answers once per row; one that does not answers once.
    let mut multiplicity = 1usize;
    for check in &prepared.checks {
        let tuples = tuples_of(catalog, &check.relation);
        let count = TupleView::new(tuples, check.filter.clone(), Vec::new()).count();
        let copies = if R::KEEPS_DUPLICATES {
            count
        } else {
            count.min(1)
        };
        multiplicity = multiplicity.saturating_mul(copies);
    }

    let relations: Vec<R> = prepared
        .indexes
        .iter()
        .zip(&prepared.index_rows)
        .map(|(spec, &rows)| {
            let base = catalog.header(&spec.relation).expect(CATALOG_HOLDS);
            let view = spec.view(tuples_of(catalog, &spec.relation));
            debug_assert_eq!(view.count(), rows, "the catalog changed since `prepare`");
            construct(spec_header(spec, base), view)
        })
        .collect();

    Indexes {
        specs: prepared.indexes.clone(),
        relations,
        multiplicity,
        rows: prepared.index_rows.iter().sum(),
    }
}

/// [`build_with`] constructing each index with [`Relation::from_view`].
///
/// # Panics
///
/// As [`build_with`].
pub fn build<R: Relation>(catalog: &Catalog, prepared: &Prepared) -> Indexes<R> {
    build_with(catalog, prepared, R::from_view)
}
```

```rust
    /// `query` prepared over `catalog` by `planner`, built as `R` and joined by `JA`, with the
    /// rows sorted.
    fn join_with<R: Relation, JA: JoinAlgo<R>>(
        catalog: &Catalog, query: &JoinQuery, planner: &Planner,
    ) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {
        let prepared = prepare(catalog, query, planner).expect("a valid query");
        let indexes = build::<R>(catalog, &prepared);
        let mut rows = Vec::new();
        execute::<R, JA>(&prepared, &indexes, |row| rows.push(row.to_vec()));
        rows.sort();
        rows
    }

    /// The sorted answer of `text` (`TreeTrie` under `LeapfrogTriejoin`), then its hash answer
    /// (`HashTrie` under `HashTriejoin`), both planned in canonical order.
    fn answers(catalog: &Catalog, text: &str) -> (Vec<Vec<usize>>, Vec<Vec<usize>>) {
        let query = parse(text);
        (
            join_with::<TreeTrie, LeapfrogTriejoin>(catalog, &query, &lexicographic()),
            join_with::<HashTrie, HashTriejoin>(catalog, &query, &lexicographic()),
        )
    }

    /// Asserts that both families answer `text` with `expected`.
    fn assert_answers(catalog: &Catalog, text: &str, expected: Vec<Vec<usize>>) {
        let (sorted, hashed) = answers(catalog, text);
        assert_eq!(sorted, expected, "TreeTrie, LeapfrogTriejoin: {text}");
        assert_eq!(hashed, expected, "HashTrie, HashTriejoin: {text}");
    }

            ("t", 3, vec![vec![1, 5, 1], vec![1, 5, 2], vec![2, 6, 2], vec![3, 5, 3]]),
        ]);
        // A constant keeps the rows that hold it.
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X) :- p(X, c10).", vec![vec![1]]);
        // A repeated variable keeps the diagonal.
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X, X).", vec![vec![1], vec![3]]);
        // Both on one atom: column 1 is 5 and column 0 equals column 2.
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X) :- t(X, c5, X).", vec![vec![1], vec![3]]);
        // Two reads of one relation: the diagonal joined with the whole relation.
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X, Y) :- r(X, X), r(X, Y).", vec![
            vec![1, 1],
            vec![1, 2],
            vec![3, 3],
        ]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn placeholders_keep_bag_semantics_and_the_head_projects() {
        let c = catalog(vec![
            ("r", 2, vec![vec![1, 2], vec![1, 3], vec![2, 4]]),
            ("t", 3, vec![vec![1, 2, 3], vec![1, 4, 3], vec![2, 5, 6]]),
        ]);
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X, _).", vec![vec![1], vec![1], vec![2]]);
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X, Z) :- t(X, _, Z).", vec![vec![1, 3], vec![1, 3], vec![2, 6]]);
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X, Y).", vec![vec![1], vec![1], vec![2]]);
    }

    /// The three atoms read one merged index.
    #[test]
    fn a_self_join_reads_one_index_for_every_atom() {
        let edges = vec![vec![1, 2], vec![2, 3], vec![1, 3], vec![3, 4], vec![2, 4]];
        let c = catalog(vec![("e", 2, edges)]);
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X, Y, Z) :- e(X, Y), e(Y, Z), e(X, Z).", vec![
            vec![1, 2, 3],
            vec![2, 3, 4],
        ]);
    }

    /// An atom against the stored column order, and the two-cycle `stored` refused, run over
    /// reversed indexes.
    #[test]
    fn a_reversed_atom_joins_through_its_own_index() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("edge", 2, vec![vec![1, 2], vec![3, 4]])]);
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X, Y) :- edge(Y, X).", vec![vec![2, 1], vec![4, 3]]);

        let c = catalog(vec![("edge", 2, vec![vec![1, 2], vec![2, 1], vec![2, 3]])]);
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X, Y) :- edge(X, Y), edge(Y, X).", vec![vec![1, 2], vec![2, 1]]);
    }

    /// `s(c7, c8)` holds twice and `t(c5)` three times: hash tries answer six times over,
    /// sorted tries once. A check that holds nowhere leaves no answer on either.
    #[test]
    fn all_constant_atoms_multiply_the_answer_on_hash_tries_only() {
        let c = catalog(vec![
            ("r", 1, vec![vec![1], vec![2]]),
            ("s", 2, vec![vec![7, 8], vec![7, 8], vec![9, 9]]),
            ("t", 1, vec![vec![5], vec![5], vec![5]]),
        ]);
        let (sorted, hashed) = answers(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X), s(c7, c8), t(c5).");
        assert_eq!(sorted, vec![vec![1], vec![2]]);
        let mut copies = vec![vec![1]; 6];
        copies.extend(vec![vec![2]; 6]);
        assert_eq!(hashed, copies);

        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X) :- r(X), s(c7, c9).", vec![]);
    }

    /// When every atom is a check there is nothing to join: the empty head row is emitted once
    /// per unit of multiplicity. The parser cannot write an empty head, so the query is built
    /// by clearing one.
    #[test]
    fn a_query_with_no_atom_left_emits_the_empty_head_per_unit_of_multiplicity() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("s", 2, vec![vec![7, 8], vec![7, 8], vec![9, 9]])]);
        let mut query = parse("Q(X) :- s(c7, c8).");
        query.head.terms.clear();
        assert!(prepare(&c, &query, &lexicographic()).unwrap().query().body.is_empty());

        let sorted = join_with::<TreeTrie, LeapfrogTriejoin>(&c, &query, &lexicographic());
        assert_eq!(sorted, vec![Vec::<usize>::new()]);
        let hashed = join_with::<HashTrie, HashTriejoin>(&c, &query, &lexicographic());
        assert_eq!(hashed, vec![Vec::<usize>::new(); 2]);

        let mut absent = parse("Q(X) :- s(c7, c9).");
        absent.head.terms.clear();
        assert!(join_with::<HashTrie, HashTriejoin>(&c, &absent, &lexicographic()).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_relation_joins_to_nothing() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("first", 1, vec![vec![1], vec![2]]), ("nothing", 1, vec![])]);
        assert_answers(&c, "Q(X) :- first(X), nothing(X).", vec![]);
    }

    /// Every optimiser plans the query of accesses, and the plan does not change the answer.
    #[test]
    fn every_optimiser_plans_over_the_accesses() {
        let c = catalog_at(StatisticsLevel::ColumnDistinct, statistics_relations());
        let query = parse(STATISTICS_QUERY);
        let expected = vec![vec![1, 2], vec![1, 2], vec![1, 3], vec![1, 3]];
        let planners = [
            planner_of(LexicographicOptimiser),
            planner_of(CardinalityOptimiser),
            planner_of(CostBasedOptimiser::default()),
        ];
        for planner in &planners {
            let sorted = join_with::<TreeTrie, LeapfrogTriejoin>(&c, &query, planner);
            assert_eq!(sorted, expected, "{planner:?}");
            let hashed = join_with::<HashTrie, HashTriejoin>(&c, &query, planner);
            assert_eq!(hashed, expected, "{planner:?}");
        }
    }

    /// Ids alone cannot tell two `Prepared` apart, since each numbers its indexes from `#0`,
    /// so `execute` compares the specs, in debug builds.
    #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "were not built from this `Prepared`")]
    fn indexes_from_another_prepared_are_refused() {
        let c = catalog(vec![("p", 2, vec![vec![1, 10], vec![2, 20]])]);
        let first = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X) :- p(X, c10).");
        let second = prepared_for(&c, "Q(X) :- p(X, c20).");
        let indexes = build::<TreeTrie>(&c, &first);
        execute::<TreeTrie, LeapfrogTriejoin>(&second, &indexes, |_| {});
    }
```

```rust
/// Joins `indexes` with `JA` and lends each answer's head to `emit`: the timed join.
///
/// `JoinAlgo::join_for_each` runs over the indexes the executed query names, and every row it
/// produces is lent to `emit` as its first [`head_len`](Prepared::head_len) values (bag
/// semantics: nothing is deduplicated). The head is emitted once per unit of
/// [`multiplicity`](Indexes::multiplicity), so a check that holds nowhere emits nothing. When
/// every atom was a check there is nothing to join, and the empty head row is emitted
/// `multiplicity` times (validation makes the head empty then, since it binds every head
/// variable in an atom).
///
/// Nothing is collected here. A lazy `HashTrie` builds the children a join reaches, through
/// `&self`, so its heap size grows with each run: measure `space` before joining.
///
/// # Panics
///
/// In debug builds, if `indexes` were not built from `prepared` (their specs differ).
pub fn execute<R, JA>(prepared: &Prepared, indexes: &Indexes<R>, mut emit: impl FnMut(&[usize]))
where
    R: JoinIterable,
    JA: JoinAlgo<R>,
{
    debug_assert_eq!(
        indexes.specs, prepared.indexes,
        "the indexes were not built from this `Prepared`"
    );
    let multiplicity = indexes.multiplicity;
    if multiplicity == 0 {
        return;
    }
    if prepared.query.body.is_empty() {
        debug_assert_eq!(prepared.head_len, 0, "a query of checks has an empty head");
        for _ in 0..multiplicity {
            emit(&[]);
        }
        return;
    }

    let ds_map: HashMap<String, &R> = prepared
        .query
        .body
        .iter()
        .map(|atom| {
            let index = indexes.get(&atom.name);
            (atom.name.clone(), index.expect("the executed query names only built indexes"))
        })
        .collect();

    // The executors emit every variable of the query they run in canonical order, and
    // `analyse` numbers the head's variables `0..head_len` in head order, so the head is each
    // row's prefix. Lending it allocates nothing.
    let head_len = prepared.head_len;
    JA::join_for_each(&prepared.plan, prepared.query.clone(), ds_map, |row| {
        let head = &row[..head_len];
        for _ in 0..multiplicity {
            emit(head);
        }
    });
}
```
