```rust
/// One benchmark, `per-query`, over `data/edge.csv` (1 -> 2, 2 -> 1,
/// 2 -> 3). A second declared relation, `data/unused.csv`, has a header that
/// parses and a row that does not, so any run that reads its tuples fails.
/// Returns the workspace and an empty cache directory.
fn per_query_workspace() -> (TempDir, TempDir) {
    let workspace = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let cache = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let data = workspace.path().join("data");
    fs::create_dir_all(&data).unwrap();
    fs::write(data.join("edge.csv"), "src,dst\n1,2\n2,1\n2,3\n").unwrap();
    fs::write(data.join("unused.csv"), "a,b\nnot,numbers\n").unwrap();
    let benchmarks = workspace.path().join("benchmarks");
    fs::create_dir_all(&benchmarks).unwrap();
    fs::write(
        benchmarks.join("per-query.yml"),
        r#"name: per-query
description: "queries over one relation, beside a relation no query names"
relations:
  - name: edge
    path: "data/edge.csv"
  - name: unused
    path: "data/unused.csv"
queries:
  - name: mutual
    description: "edges present in both directions: two indexes over one relation"
    query: "Q(X, Y) :- edge(X, Y), edge(Y, X)."
    expected: 2
  - name: pinned
    description: "the sources of edges into 2: a constant filter"
    query: "Q(X) :- edge(X, c2)."
    expected: 1
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    (workspace, cache)
}

/// `bench run per-query` in `workspace` with `args`, returning the process
/// output and the parsed report array (empty if no report was written).
fn bench_run_per_query(
    workspace: &TempDir, cache: &TempDir, args: &[&str],
) -> (Output, Vec<serde_json::Value>) {
    let report = workspace.path().join("report.json");
    let output = Command::new(kermit_bin())
        .env("RUST_BACKTRACE", "0")
        .env("RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE", "0")
        .env("KERMIT_WORKSPACE", workspace.path())
        .env("XDG_CACHE_HOME", cache.path())
        .current_dir(workspace.path())
        .args([
            "bench",
            "--sample-size",
            "10",
            "--measurement-time",
            "1",
            "--warm-up-time",
            "1",
            "--report-json",
        ])
        .arg(&report)
        .args(["run", "per-query"])
        .args(args)
        .output()
        .unwrap();
    let reports = fs::read_to_string(&report)
        .ok()
        .map(|text| serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    (output, reports)
}

/// The report's Criterion function ids, sorted.
fn functions_of(report: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut functions: Vec<String> = report["criterion_groups"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|g| g["function"].as_str().unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();
    functions.sort_unstable();
    functions
}

/// The values of the report's `index` metadata lines, in order.
fn index_lines(report: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<String> {
    report["metadata"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .filter(|m| m["label"] == "index")
        .map(|m| m["value"].as_str().unwrap().to_string())
        .collect()
}

/// `edge(X, Y), edge(Y, X)` was rejected under `--column-orders stored`
/// (contradictory orders). Every query is now planned freely and each atom
/// builds the index its plan reads: here the relation twice, in two column
/// orders. `unused.csv` is declared but never read.
#[test]
fn bench_run_builds_one_index_per_atom_and_reports_each() {
    let (workspace, cache) = per_query_workspace();
    let (output, reports) = bench_run_per_query(&workspace, &cache, &[
        "-q",
        "mutual",
        "-i",
        "tree-trie",
        "-a",
        "leapfrog-triejoin",
        "--verify",
        "-m",
        "build",
        "iteration",
        "space",
    ]);
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    assert!(output.status.success(), "{stderr}");
    assert_eq!(reports.len(), 1, "{reports:?}");
    let report = &reports[0];
    assert_eq!(functions_of(report), ["build", "iteration", "space"]);
    let axes = &report["axes"];
    assert!(axes.get("column_orders").is_none(), "{axes}");
    assert_eq!(axes["verified"], true);
    assert_eq!(
        axes["tuples"], 3,
        "the relation's rows, once, however many atoms read it"
    );
    assert_eq!(axes["index_rows"], 6, "two unfiltered indexes of three rows");
    let lines = index_lines(report);
    assert_eq!(lines.len(), 2, "{lines:?}");
    assert!(
        lines[0].starts_with("#0 edge filter - columns [0, 1]: 3 rows, "),
        "{lines:?}"
    );
    assert!(
        lines[1].starts_with("#1 edge filter - columns [1, 0]: 3 rows, "),
        "{lines:?}"
    );
    assert!(lines.iter().all(|line| line.ends_with(" bytes")), "{lines:?}");
    for line in &lines {
        assert!(stderr.contains(line.as_str()), "{line} missing from {stderr}");
    }
}

/// A lazy `HashTrie`'s joins expand it, so `--verify` and `iteration` run on
/// fresh builds (#92), `end_to_end` builds its own, and `space` must find the
/// as-built indexes untouched.
#[test]
fn bench_run_on_a_lazy_cell_runs_every_metric_over_fresh_builds() {
    let (workspace, cache) = per_query_workspace();
    let (output, reports) = bench_run_per_query(&workspace, &cache, &[
        "-q",
        "mutual",
        "-i",
        "hash-trie",
        "-a",
        "hash-triejoin",
        "--ds-layout-expansion",
        "lazy",
        "--verify",
        "-m",
        "build",
        "iteration",
        "end-to-end",
        "space",
    ]);
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    assert!(output.status.success(), "{stderr}");
    assert_eq!(reports.len(), 1, "{reports:?}");
    assert_eq!(functions_of(&reports[0]), [
        "build",
        "end_to_end",
        "iteration",
        "space"
    ]);
    assert_eq!(reports[0]["axes"]["verified"], true);
    assert_eq!(reports[0]["axes"]["ds_layout_expansion"], "lazy");
}

/// A constant is applied while the index is built: the index holds only the
/// rows that match, and its line names the filter.
#[test]
fn bench_run_pushes_a_constant_into_the_index_it_builds() {
    let (workspace, cache) = per_query_workspace();
    let (output, reports) = bench_run_per_query(&workspace, &cache, &[
        "-q",
        "pinned",
        "-i",
        "tree-trie",
        "-a",
        "leapfrog-triejoin",
        "--verify",
        "-m",
        "space",
    ]);
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    assert!(output.status.success(), "{stderr}");
    let report = &reports[0];
    assert_eq!(report["axes"]["verified"], true);
    assert_eq!(
        report["axes"]["tuples"], 3,
        "tuples counts the catalog's rows, not the filtered ones"
    );
    assert_eq!(report["axes"]["index_rows"], 1);
    let lines = index_lines(report);
    assert_eq!(lines.len(), 1, "{lines:?}");
    assert!(
        lines[0].starts_with("#0 edge filter col1=2 columns [0]: 1 rows, "),
        "{lines:?}"
    );
}

/// `unused.csv` cannot be read, and the run succeeds: no query names it, so

fn bench_run_reads_only_the_relations_its_queries_name() {
```

```rust
/// Everything a measured join needs besides the cell and the workload:
/// what kind of report to stamp, how to name the Criterion group, which
/// optimiser the report names, and what to measure. One value is built
/// per subcommand invocation and shared by every cell it runs.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct RunSettings<'a> {
    /// The report's `kind` field (`Run` for `bench run`, `Join` for
    /// `bench join`); the group naming is the same for both.
    pub kind: BenchKind,
    /// First segment of the Criterion group
    /// (`{prefix}/{workload}/{query}/{ds}/{algo}`), from `--name` or the
    /// subcommand's default.
    pub prefix: &'a str,
    /// `--optimiser`, for the report's `optimiser` axis. The queries were
    /// planned when the workload was prepared, so nothing here plans.
    pub planner: PlannerArgs,
    pub metrics: &'a [Metric],
    /// K in the `end_to_end` metric's `T = build + K × query`.
    pub queries_per_build: u32,
    /// Run each query once before timing and compare its tuple count with
    /// the workload's `expected`; a mismatch aborts.
    pub verify: bool,
    /// Criterion sample/measurement/warm-up settings.
    pub bench_args: &'a BenchArgs,
}
```

Second, replace `run_benchmark` with the three items below: from its doc comment (`/// Runs every query of `workload` on one execution cell and returns one`, line 63) through the closing `}` of the function (line 487, the line before `/// Runs one `bench run` cell by monomorphising [`run_benchmark`] over the`):

```rust
/// The value of one `index` metadata line, for the `position`th index of a
/// query: `{id} {relation} filter {filter} columns {columns:?}: {rows} rows,
/// {bytes} bytes`. `rows` is what the build copied, the index view's count,
/// and `bytes` the index's footprint as built.
fn describe_index(position: usize, spec: &IndexSpec, rows: usize, bytes: usize) -> String {
    format!(
        "{INDEX_ID_PREFIX}{position} {} filter {} columns {:?}: {rows} rows, {bytes} bytes",
        spec.relation, spec.filter, spec.columns
    )
}

/// The rows the relations `prepared` reads hold in `catalog`, each relation
/// counted once however many atoms read it: the report's `tuples` axis, the
/// same for every structure.
fn tuples_read(catalog: &Catalog, prepared: &Prepared) -> usize {
    prepared
        .relations()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|name| catalog.tuples(name).map_or(0, Tuples::len))
        .sum()
}

/// Runs every query of `workload` on one execution cell and returns one
/// report per query, each stamped with `settings.kind` and grouped under
/// `settings.prefix`.
///
/// Generic over the [`ExecutionFamily`] so the sorted family
/// (`TrieLftj<R>`) and the hash family (`HashHtj<H, P, E>`) share one body:
/// metadata, Criterion group wiring and report assembly are identical, and
/// the report's `data_structure` / `algorithm` axes come from
/// `family.execution()` — the same value that picked the code path — so a
/// report can never name an algorithm it did not run (issue #56).
///
/// The workload arrives prepared (`Workload::prepare`): every query is
/// validated and planned, and the relations the queries name sit in the
/// catalog as flat tuples, so a query that cannot run never reaches this
/// function (issue #78). Per query, the cell builds exactly the indexes the
/// plan reads (`ExecutionFamily::build_indexes`). One build, untimed, backs
/// the `index` metadata, `space` and a non-mutating `iteration`; `build`
/// and `end_to_end` time fresh ones, and a family whose joins mutate their
/// indexes (`ExecutionFamily::JOIN_MUTATES`) also joins over fresh ones for
/// `iteration` and `--verify`. Every timed routine returns what it built, so
/// Criterion frees it after the timer stops. With `settings.verify`, each
/// query with an `expected` count is executed once before timing and a
/// mismatch aborts.
fn run_benchmark<F: ExecutionFamily>(
    family: &F, workload: &PreparedWorkload, settings: RunSettings<'_>,
) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<BenchReport>> {
    let RunSettings {
        kind,
        prefix,
        planner,
        metrics,
        queries_per_build,
        verify,
        bench_args,
    } = settings;
    let PreparedWorkload {
        workload: definition,
        catalog,
        prepared: prepared_queries,
    } = workload;

    // `ds_name`/`algo_name` become the report's identity axes and the
    // on-disk `target/criterion/{group}` names (the group_name below embeds
    // them). The labels are pinned by `IndexStructure::axis_value` and
    // `JoinAlgorithm::axis_value`; see the tests there before changing one.
    let execution = family.execution();
    let ds_name = execution.index_structure().axis_value();
    let algo_name = execution.algorithm().axis_value();

    let has_time_metrics = metrics
        .iter()
        .any(|m| matches!(m, Metric::Build | Metric::Iteration | Metric::EndToEnd));

    // Standard optimization axes: the dimensions the structure emits (the
    // `ds_*` prefix convention, see `kermit_iters::HasOptimizationAxes`,
    // guarantees no collision with the base axes assembled per query below)
    // plus the build mode, which comes from the family because it leaves no
    // trace in the structure. They are read off one empty relation, since
    // they depend on the type, not on the data, and a query whose atoms are
    // all constant checks builds no index to read them from.
    let optimization_axes = {
        let empty = Tuples::new(1);
        let probe = family.build_index(
            RelationHeader::new_positional("axes", 1),
            TupleView::all(&empty),
        );
        let mut axes = F::optimization_axes(&probe);
        axes.extend(family.build_mode_axes());
        axes
    };

    let mut reports: Vec<BenchReport> = Vec::with_capacity(definition.queries.len());

    for (query_def, prepared) in definition.queries.iter().zip(prepared_queries) {
        // This query's indexes, built once and untimed: the `index` metadata
        // and `space` describe them, and a family whose joins leave an index
        // as built (`iteration`, `--verify`) joins over them.
        let indexes = family.build_indexes(catalog, prepared);
        // A family whose joins mutate their indexes (a lazy HashTrie expands
        // what a join reaches, #92) never probes these: `--verify` and
        // `iteration` run on fresh builds, so `space` measures the indexes as
        // built, whatever ran before it. Their footprint now is what the
        // `space` block checks against.
        let as_built_bytes: Option<Vec<usize>> = F::JOIN_MUTATES
            .then(|| indexes.iter().map(|(_, index)| index.heap_size_bytes()).collect());

        let mut metadata = vec![
            MetadataLine::new("benchmark", &definition.name),
            MetadataLine::new("query", &query_def.name),
            MetadataLine::new("data structure", ds_name),
            MetadataLine::new("algorithm", algo_name),
            MetadataLine::new("allocator", crate::ALLOCATOR),
        ];
        for (position, (spec, index)) in indexes.iter().enumerate() {
            let source = catalog
                .tuples(&spec.relation)
                .expect("prepare checked that every indexed relation is in the catalog");
            let rows = spec.view(source).count();
            metadata.push(MetadataLine::new(
                "index",
                describe_index(position, spec, rows, index.heap_size_bytes()),
            ));
        }
        // Correctness gate: with `--verify`, run the query once (untimed)
        // and compare the answer count before spending any measurement time
        // on it. A mismatch aborts so a wrong answer can never yield a
        // plausible timing. The count comes through the same streaming path
        // the `iteration` metric times, so verifying a huge result never
        // materialises it.
        let verified = if verify {
            match query_def.expected {
                | Some(expected) => {
                    let actual = if F::JOIN_MUTATES {
                        let fresh = family.build_indexes(catalog, prepared);
                        family.count_rows(prepared, &fresh)
                    } else {
                        family.count_rows(prepared, &indexes)
                    };
                    if actual != expected {
                        anyhow::bail!(
                            "verification failed: benchmark '{}' query '{}' on {}/{} returned {} \
                             tuples, expected {}",
                            definition.name,
                            query_def.name,
                            ds_name,
                            algo_name,
                            actual,
                            expected
                        );
                    }
                    metadata.push(MetadataLine::new("verified", "yes"));
                    true
                },
                | None => {
                    eprintln!(
                        "bench run: no expected cardinality for query '{}' in benchmark '{}'; not \
                         verified",
                        query_def.name, definition.name
                    );
                    false
                },
            }
        } else {
            false
        };
        if metrics.contains(&Metric::EndToEnd) {
            metadata.push(MetadataLine::new("queries per build", queries_per_build));
        }
        for name in prepared.relations() {
            if let Some(header) = catalog.header(name) {
                metadata.push(MetadataLine::new(
                    "relation",
                    format!("{:?} (arity {})", header.name(), header.arity()),
                ));
            }
        }
        write_metadata_block(&mut io::stderr(), "bench run metadata", &metadata)?;

        let group_name =
            criterion_group_name(prefix, &definition.name, &query_def.name, execution);

        let mut criterion_groups: Vec<CriterionGroupRef> = Vec::new();

        if has_time_metrics {
            let mut criterion = build_time_criterion(bench_args);
            let mut group = criterion.benchmark_group(&group_name);

            if metrics.contains(&Metric::Build) {
                // Times `build_indexes` alone: every index this query's plan
                // reads and its constant checks, each copied once from the
                // catalog's flat tuples, through the same `build_index` that
                // honours the configuration and build mode the report's
                // `ds_config_*` / `ds_build_mode` axes name. Planning is done
                // and statistics are gathered, so neither is in the timer.
                // The setup is a no-op and the routine returns the indexes,
                // so nothing is copied beforehand, Criterion drops them after
                // the timer stops, and `PerIteration` keeps one set alive at
                // a time.
                group.bench_function("build", |b| {
                    b.iter_batched(
                        || (),
                        |()| family.build_indexes(catalog, prepared),
                        criterion::BatchSize::PerIteration,
                    );
                });
                criterion_groups.push(CriterionGroupRef {
                    group: group_name.clone(),
                    function: "build".to_string(),
                    metric: ReportMetric::Time,
                });
            }

            if metrics.contains(&Metric::Iteration) {
                // Times the join with its rows counted, never collected: the
                // timed region holds no per-row allocation, and only a `u64`
                // stays alive, so memory is independent of result size
                // (issue #65).
                if F::JOIN_MUTATES {
                    // Cold (#92): each timed join runs on indexes built in
                    // the untimed setup, so it pays the expansion its own
                    // probes cause instead of finding it done by an earlier
                    // sample. The routine hands the indexes back, so
                    // Criterion drops them after timing, and `PerIteration`
                    // keeps one fresh set alive at a time.
                    group.bench_function("iteration", |b| {
                        b.iter_batched(
                            || family.build_indexes(catalog, prepared),
                            |fresh| {
                                let rows = family.count_rows(prepared, &fresh);
                                (fresh, rows)
                            },
                            criterion::BatchSize::PerIteration,
                        );
                    });
                } else {
                    group.bench_function("iteration", |b| {
                        b.iter(|| family.count_rows(prepared, &indexes));
                    });
                }
                criterion_groups.push(CriterionGroupRef {
                    group: group_name.clone(),
                    function: "iteration".to_string(),
                    metric: ReportMetric::Time,
                });
            }

            if metrics.contains(&Metric::EndToEnd) {
                // The timed body is the `build` metric's `build_indexes`
                // followed by K joins over the indexes it built, so the
                // build term is the one the `iteration` metric's indexes
                // paid and the whole equals `build` + K × `iteration`.
                //
                // PerIteration: a fresh build per sample is the point of this
                // metric — batching would amortise away the construction cost
                // whose interaction with query traversal is under measurement.
                // The routine returns the indexes, so they are freed outside
                // the timer.
                group.bench_function("end_to_end", |b| {
                    b.iter_batched(
                        || (),
                        |()| {
                            let built = family.build_indexes(catalog, prepared);
                            for _ in 0..queries_per_build {
                                std::hint::black_box(family.count_rows(prepared, &built));
                            }
                            built
                        },
                        criterion::BatchSize::PerIteration,
                    );
                });
                criterion_groups.push(CriterionGroupRef {
                    group: group_name.clone(),
                    function: "end_to_end".to_string(),
                    metric: ReportMetric::Time,
                });
            }

            group.finish();
            criterion.final_summary();
        }

        if metrics.contains(&Metric::Space) {
            let built: Vec<&F::Rel> = indexes.iter().map(|(_, index)| index).collect();
            if let Some(as_built) = &as_built_bytes {
                let now: Vec<usize> = built.iter().map(|index| index.heap_size_bytes()).collect();
                anyhow::ensure!(
                    now == *as_built,
                    "internal error: a probe reached the indexes of a {ds_name} cell whose joins \
                     mutate their relations, so `space` would measure them partly expanded; see \
                     `ExecutionFamily::JOIN_MUTATES`"
                );
            }
            // A query whose atoms are all constant checks builds no index,
            // and there is nothing to measure.
            if !built.is_empty() {
                let mut criterion = build_space_criterion(bench_args);
                let mut group = criterion.benchmark_group(&group_name);
                // One function per query, summing every index it reads.
                criterion_groups.push(add_space_bench(
                    &mut group,
                    &group_name,
                    "space".to_string(),
                    &built,
                ));
                group.finish();
                criterion.final_summary();
            }
        }

        let mut axes = BTreeMap::from([
            ("benchmark".to_string(), serde_json::json!(definition.name)),
            ("query".to_string(), serde_json::json!(query_def.name)),
            ("data_structure".to_string(), serde_json::json!(ds_name)),
            ("algorithm".to_string(), serde_json::json!(algo_name)),
            (
                "optimiser".to_string(),
                serde_json::json!(planner.optimiser.axis_value()),
            ),
            (
                "tuples".to_string(),
                serde_json::json!(tuples_read(catalog, prepared)),
            ),
            (
                "index_rows".to_string(),
                serde_json::json!(indexes.rows()),
            ),
        ]);
        // Only meaningful when the end-to-end metric ran; omitting it
        // otherwise keeps historical invocations' reports unchanged.
        if metrics.contains(&Metric::EndToEnd) {
            axes.insert(
                "queries_per_build".to_string(),
                serde_json::json!(queries_per_build),
            );
        }
        axes.extend(optimization_axes.clone());
        if verified {
            axes.insert("verified".to_string(), serde_json::json!(true));
        }
        reports.push(BenchReport::new(kind, &metadata, axes, criterion_groups));
    }

    Ok(reports)
}
```

## Story 18: `kermit join` and `bench join --output` share the prepared workload, and `--column-orders` goes

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit/src/main.rs`, `kermit/src/options.rs`, `kermit/src/execution.rs`, `kermit/tests/cli_query_errors.rs`, `kermit/tests/cli_hash_trie_build_mode.rs`
- **Interfaces:** uses Story 17's `PreparedWorkload`; removes `--column-orders` (Names contract: the binary)
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit --test cli_query_errors`
- **Review:** deep

`kermit join` and `bench join --output` stop building an engine of their own. Both go through
`Workload::adhoc(…).prepare(…)`, which validates from headers, reads only the relations the
query names into one `Catalog` and plans the query once. The CSV comes from the cell's family
(`build_indexes`, then `execute` into the `CsvSink`), and `bench join` hands the very same
`PreparedWorkload` to `dispatch_run_bench`, so its relations are read once for the CSV and the
benchmark together. `validate_query_files` goes, since `prepare` validates. `--column-orders`
leaves `PlannerArgs`: a query now builds each index in its plan's column order, so there is
nothing left for the flag to choose, and `instantiate` plans over any order
(`ColumnOrderPolicy::Any`) until Story 23 deletes the policy type. The query
`edge(X, Y), edge(Y, X)`, which `stored` rejected as a limitation, now runs, so
`cli_query_errors.rs` swaps its cyclic-order shape for a positive test. Once the old runner is
gone, some of the old `RelationFamily` / `ExecutionFamily` items in `execution.rs` have no caller
left, so Task 18.2 marks exactly those `#[allow(dead_code)] // Unused until Story 19`, the story
that deletes them. Neither task's code holds a landmine marker. The work splits in two so that each task leaves the tree green: Task 18.1
removes the flag while the old runner keeps working (as the `any` path it already was), and
Task 18.2 replaces the runner, and rewords the one test comment that named it.

### Task 18.1: Remove `--column-orders`

**Files:**
- Modify: `kermit/src/options.rs:1-4`, `kermit/src/options.rs:18-44`, `kermit/src/options.rs:2052-2078`
- Modify: `kermit/src/main.rs:562`, `kermit/src/main.rs:591`
- Test: `kermit/tests/cli_query_errors.rs:303-316`, `kermit/src/options.rs` (inline `mod tests`)

```rust
/// Mutual edges need `edge` in two column orders: a limitation, which
/// used to panic in the planner.
#[test]
fn cyclic_attribute_order_is_a_reported_limitation() {
    assert_rejected_everywhere(
```

with:

```rust
/// A relation with a mutual pair (1 and 2), a one-way edge and a self-loop.
const MUTUAL_EDGES: &str = "src,dst\n1,2\n2,1\n2,3\n3,3\n";

/// Both `edge(X, Y)` and `edge(Y, X)` hold. The query reads `edge` in two
/// column orders, which `--column-orders stored` rejected as a limitation;
/// every query now builds each index in its plan's order, so it just runs.
const MUTUAL_QUERY: &str = "Q(X, Y) :- edge(X, Y), edge(Y, X).";

/// [`MUTUAL_QUERY`]'s answer over [`MUTUAL_EDGES`], sorted.
const MUTUAL_ROWS: [&str; 3] = ["1,2", "2,1", "3,3"];

/// Writes [`MUTUAL_EDGES`] and [`MUTUAL_QUERY`] into `dir`; returns their paths.
fn write_mutual_fixture(dir: &Path) -> (PathBuf, PathBuf) {
    let edge = dir.join("edge.csv");
    fs::write(&edge, MUTUAL_EDGES).unwrap();
    let query = dir.join("mutual.dl");
    fs::write(&query, MUTUAL_QUERY).unwrap();
    (edge, query)
}

/// Splits CSV output into its header line and its data lines, sorted (the
/// hash family's row order is unspecified).
fn header_and_sorted_rows(csv: &str) -> (&str, Vec<&str>) {
    let mut lines = csv.lines();
    let header = lines.next().expect("a header line");
    let mut rows: Vec<&str> = lines.collect();
    rows.sort_unstable();
    (header, rows)
}

/// The mutual-edge query needs `edge` in two column orders. It used to be
/// rejected as a limitation; now it runs, with the same answer, on every cell.
#[test]
fn mutual_edges_run_on_every_cell() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let (edge, query) = write_mutual_fixture(dir.path());
    for cell in CELLS {
        let output = Command::new(kermit_bin())
            .env("RUST_BACKTRACE", "0")
            .env("RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE", "0")
            .arg("join")
            .arg("-r")
            .arg(&edge)
            .arg("-q")
            .arg(&query)
            .args(cell)
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{cell:?}: {stderr}");
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
        let (header, rows) = header_and_sorted_rows(&stdout);
        assert_eq!(header, "X,Y", "{cell:?}");
        assert_eq!(rows, MUTUAL_ROWS, "{cell:?}");
    }
}

/// `--column-orders` is gone from `join` and `bench join` (and `bench run`,
/// which shares `PlannerArgs`): clap rejects it as an unknown argument.
#[test]
fn column_orders_flag_is_gone() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let (edge, query) = write_mutual_fixture(dir.path());
    let report = dir.path().join("report.json");
    let edge = edge.to_str().unwrap();
    let query = query.to_str().unwrap();
    let report = report.to_str().unwrap();
    let invocations: [Vec<&str>; 2] = [
        vec![
            "join",
            "-r",
            edge,
            "-q",
            query,
            "-i",
            "tree-trie",
            "-a",
            "leapfrog-triejoin",
            "--column-orders",
            "any",
        ],
        vec![
            "bench",
            "--report-json",
            report,
            "join",
            "-r",
            edge,
            "-q",
            query,
            "-i",
            "tree-trie",
            "-a",
            "leapfrog-triejoin",
            "-m",
            "space",
            "--column-orders",
            "any",
        ],
    ];
    for args in &invocations {
        let output = Command::new(kermit_bin())
            .env("RUST_BACKTRACE", "0")
            .args(args)
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
```

```rust
/// How a join is planned: the optimiser and the column-order policy.
/// Flattened into `join`, `bench join` and `bench run`; `bench ds` joins
/// nothing and has neither flag.
#[derive(Args, Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct PlannerArgs {
    /// Query optimiser (plans the join's variable ordering). Long-only:
    /// `-o` belongs to `--output`.
    #[arg(long, value_enum, default_value_t = Optimiser::Lexicographic)]
    pub(crate) optimiser: Optimiser,

    /// Column orders the planner may bind an atom's columns in: `stored`
    /// reads each relation in its stored column order, so a plan binds
    /// every atom's columns left to right; `any` lets the planner choose,
    /// and an atom whose plan disagrees with the stored order runs over a
    /// per-query copy with the columns permuted, built before the timed
    /// join (`copies`) and dropped after the query.
    #[arg(long, value_enum, default_value_t = ColumnOrderPolicy::Stored)]
    pub(crate) column_orders: ColumnOrderPolicy,
}

impl PlannerArgs {
    /// The planner these flags select. A `Planner` owns its optimiser, so
    /// each family gets its own.
    pub(crate) fn instantiate(self) -> Planner {
        Planner::new(self.optimiser.instantiate(), self.column_orders)
    }
}
```

```rust
fn join_reads_only_the_relations_the_query_names() {

    let (edge, query) = write_mutual_fixture(dir.path());
    let bad = write_unreadable_unnamed_relation(dir.path());
    for cell in [CELLS[0], CELLS[2]] {
        let output = Command::new(kermit_bin())
            .env("RUST_BACKTRACE", "0")
            .env("RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE", "0")

            .output()
            .unwrap();

        let (header, rows) = header_and_sorted_rows(&stdout);

/// `bench join --output` writes the CSV and runs the benchmark from one
/// prepared workload: the CSV holds the answer, and the report names the
/// same query and cell. The unnamed unreadable relation is never loaded
/// for either.
#[test]
fn bench_join_output_and_benchmark_share_one_prepared_workload() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let (edge, query) = write_mutual_fixture(dir.path());
    let bad = write_unreadable_unnamed_relation(dir.path());
    for (structure, algorithm) in [
        ("tree-trie", "leapfrog-triejoin"),
        ("column-trie", "leapfrog-triejoin"),
        ("hash-trie", "hash-triejoin"),
    ] {
        let csv = dir.path().join(format!("{structure}.csv"));
        let report = dir.path().join(format!("{structure}.json"));
        let output = Command::new(kermit_bin())
            .env("RUST_BACKTRACE", "0")
            .env("RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE", "0")
            .args([
                "bench",
                "--sample-size",
                "10",
                "--measurement-time",
                "1",
                "--warm-up-time",
                "1",
                "--report-json",
            ])
            .arg(&report)
            .arg("join")
            .arg("--relations")
            .arg(&edge)
            .arg(&bad)
            .arg("--query")
            .arg(&query)
            .args(["-i", structure, "-a", algorithm, "-m", "space", "--output"])
            .arg(&csv)
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{structure}: {stderr}");

        let text = fs::read_to_string(&csv).unwrap();
        let (header, rows) = header_and_sorted_rows(&text);
        assert_eq!(header, "X,Y", "{structure}");
        assert_eq!(rows, MUTUAL_ROWS, "{structure}");

        let reports: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&fs::read_to_string(&report).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let axes = &reports[0]["axes"];
        assert_eq!(axes["query"], "mutual", "{structure}");
        assert_eq!(axes["benchmark"], "adhoc", "{structure}");
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Reads and plans the one query of `args`: the query file is parsed,
/// validated against every header in `args.relations`, and prepared over a
/// catalog of the relations it names (`Workload::prepare`). `kermit join`
/// and `bench join` (its CSV and its benchmark alike) share the result, so
/// the relations are read once.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// The query file cannot be read or parsed, a relation file cannot be
/// read, or validation rejects the query, before any index is built.
fn prepare_query(args: &QueryArgs) -> anyhow::Result<PreparedWorkload> {
    Workload::adhoc(args.relations.clone(), &args.query)?.prepare(&args.planner.instantiate())
}

/// Builds the indexes of `workload`'s one query on `family` and streams the
/// join to `writer` as CSV: the header row, then one line per tuple as the
/// join produces it, so writing a result never materialises it. `workload`
/// comes from [`prepare_query`], so it holds exactly one query.
fn write_prepared_join<F: ExecutionFamily>(
    family: F, cell: Execution, workload: &PreparedWorkload, writer: impl Write,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // The joins this writes (`kermit join`, `bench join --output`) produce
    // CSV, not a report axis, and every Layout gives the same answers, so
    // this is the only check that a dispatch arm monomorphised the cell it
    // was asked for: `execution` re-derives the Layout labels from the
    // family's type parameters.
    debug_assert_eq!(
        family.execution(),
        cell,
        "dispatch built a different cell than the one resolved"
    );
    let query = &workload.workload.queries[0].query;
    let prepared = &workload.prepared[0];
    let indexes = family.build_indexes(&workload.catalog, prepared);
    let mut sink = CsvSink::new(writer, &head_column_names(query))?;
    family.execute(prepared, &indexes, |tuple| sink.write_tuple(tuple));
    sink.finish()?;
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
/// Writes `workload`'s one query, run on `cell`'s family, to `writer` as
/// CSV. `bench join --output` passes the very cell its measurements run, so
/// the CSV comes from the same kind of build.
fn write_query_csv(
    cell: Execution, planner_args: PlannerArgs, workload: &PreparedWorkload, writer: impl Write,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // One planner per family: a `Planner` owns its optimiser.
    let planner = || planner_args.instantiate();
    match cell {
        | Execution::TrieLftj(SortedTrie::TreeTrie {
            seek,
            build,
        }) => with_sorted_trie_layout!(seek, |S| write_prepared_join(
            TrieLftj::<kermit_ds::TreeTrie<S>>::new(build, planner()),
            cell,
            workload,
            writer,
        )),
        | Execution::TrieLftj(SortedTrie::ColumnTrie {
            seek,
            build,
        }) => with_sorted_trie_layout!(seek, |S| write_prepared_join(
            TrieLftj::<kermit_ds::ColumnTrie<S>>::new(build, planner()),
            cell,
            workload,
            writer,
        )),
        | Execution::HashHtj {
            hasher,
            pruning,
            expansion,
            config,
            build,
        } => with_hash_trie_layout!(hasher, pruning, expansion, |H, P, E| write_prepared_join(
            HashHtj::<H, P, E>::new(config, build, planner()),
            cell,
            workload,
            writer,
        )),
    }
}
```

```rust
fn run_join(query_args: QueryArgs, output: Option<PathBuf>) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let join_query = parse_query(&query_args)?;
    validate_query_files(&join_query, &query_args)?;
    // `kermit join` has no `--ds-config` / `--ds-build` (neither can change
    // an answer), so it resolves its layout flags against their defaults,
    // through the same validator as every bench command.
    let choices = DsChoices::resolve(
        IndexStructureSelector::of(query_args.indexstructure),
        &query_args.layout,
        &ConfigChoices::default(),
        &BuildChoices::default(),

    let header = head_column_names(&join_query);
    let writer: Box<dyn Write> = match &output {
        | Some(path) => Box::new(BufWriter::new(fs::File::create(path)?)),
        | None => Box::new(BufWriter::new(io::stdout().lock())),
    };
    write_join(writer, &header, &mut join, join_query)
```

Replace the function body (keep the signature and its doc comment) with the version below. The

```rust
fn run_join(query_args: QueryArgs, output: Option<PathBuf>) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // `kermit join` has no `--ds-config` / `--ds-build` (neither can change
    // an answer), so it resolves its layout flags against their defaults,
    // through the same validator as every bench command.
    let choices = DsChoices::resolve(
        IndexStructureSelector::of(query_args.indexstructure),
        &query_args.layout,
        &ConfigChoices::default(),
        &BuildChoices::default(),
    )?;
    let cell = query_cell(&query_args, choices)?;
    let workload = prepare_query(&query_args)?;
    let writer: Box<dyn Write> = match &output {
        | Some(path) => Box::new(BufWriter::new(fs::File::create(path)?)),
        | None => Box::new(BufWriter::new(io::stdout().lock())),
    };
    write_query_csv(cell, query_args.planner, &workload, writer)
}
```

```rust
/// Handler for `bench join`: an ad-hoc workload over the given relation
/// files, run through the same generic runner as `bench run` under the
/// `adhoc/{query-stem}` identity. The CSV (`--output`) and the benchmark
/// share one prepared workload, so the relations are read once.
fn run_bench_join(
    bench_args: &BenchArgs, query_args: QueryArgs, output: Option<PathBuf>, metrics: &[Metric],
    queries_per_build: u32, config: ConfigChoices, build: BuildChoices,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let selector = IndexStructureSelector::of(query_args.indexstructure);
    let choices = DsChoices::resolve(selector, &query_args.layout, &config, &build)?;
    let cell = query_cell(&query_args, choices)?;
    let workload = prepare_query(&query_args)?;

    if let Some(path) = &output {
        let writer = BufWriter::new(fs::File::create(path)?);
        write_query_csv(cell, query_args.planner, &workload, writer)?;
    }

    let settings = RunSettings {
        kind: BenchKind::Join,
        prefix: bench_args.name.as_deref().unwrap_or(DEFAULT_JOIN_GROUP),
        planner: query_args.planner,
        metrics,
        queries_per_build,
        verify: false,
        bench_args,
    };
    let mut sink = ReportSink::open(bench_args.report_json.as_deref(), BenchKind::Join)?;
    let reports = dispatch_run_bench(cell, &workload, settings)?;
    sink.push(reports)?;
    sink.finish()?;
    Ok(())
}
```

## Story 19: Families lose the old engine API

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit/src/execution.rs`, `kermit/src/bench/run.rs`, `kermit/src/main.rs`, `kermit/tests/cli_hash_trie_config_choice.rs`
- **Interfaces:** removes the old family API (Names contract: the binary); uses Stories 15–18
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit --bin kermit`
- **Review:** deep

After Stories 15–18 every caller builds and runs a query through `build_index`,
`build_indexes`, `execute` and `count_rows`, so the old half of the family API has no user
left. This story removes it: `RelationFamily::{build_relation, load, load_with_tuples}` and
`ExecutionFamily::{Engine, build, build_from_tuples, relations, join_for_each, count,
required_indexes, add_index, clear_indexes, indexes}`. `TrieLftj` and `HashHtj` stop holding a
`Planner`, since `prepare` runs before any family does, so their constructors become
`TrieLftj::new(build)` and `HashHtj::new(config, build)`, and the dispatch arms in `run.rs` and
`main.rs` build them without one. `ExecutionFamily::JOIN_MUTATES` stays: a lazy `HashTrie`'s
joins still build children, so `iteration` and `--verify` still run on fresh builds. The
module's tests are most of the work. Task 19.1 moves them onto the new API while the old one
still exists, so each test is proved against the code it will keep testing; Task 19.2 then
removes the old API behind a test that only compiles without a planner. No code in this story
holds a landmine marker.

### Task 19.1: Move the family tests onto `build_index`, `build_indexes` and `execute`

```rust
    /// `query` prepared over a catalog holding `tuples` as the relation
    /// `header` names: what a family's `build_indexes` and `execute` take.
    fn prepared_over(
        header: RelationHeader, tuples: Tuples, query: &str,
    ) -> (kermit::db::Catalog, kermit::db::Prepared) {
        use {
            kermit::db::{prepare, Catalog},
            kermit_algos::{
                ColumnOrderPolicy, JoinQuery, LexicographicOptimiser, Planner, StatisticsLevel,
            },
        };
        let catalog = Catalog::new(vec![(header, tuples)], StatisticsLevel::TupleCounts);
        let query: JoinQuery = query.parse().expect("the query parses");
        let planner = Planner::new(Box::new(LexicographicOptimiser), ColumnOrderPolicy::Any);
        let prepared = prepare(&catalog, &query, &planner).expect("the query prepares");
        (catalog, prepared)
    }
```

```rust
    /// The `build` metric builds through [`RelationFamily::build_index`], so
    /// it must honour the config too — otherwise it would time an
    /// unconfigured build under a report labelled with the configured axes.
    #[test]
    fn hash_family_build_index_honours_its_config() {
        let config = HashTrieConfig {
            load_factor: kermit_ds::LoadFactor::percent(50).unwrap(),
            ..HashTrieConfig::default()
        };
        let family = HashHtj::<kermit_iters::SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>::new(
            config,
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        );
        let header = RelationHeader::new("r", vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()]);
        let tuples = Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2]]);
        let rel = family.build_index(header, kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples));
        assert_eq!(*rel.config(), config);
        assert_eq!(
            HashHtj::<kermit_iters::SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>::optimization_axes(
                &rel
            )
            .get("ds_config_load_factor"),
            Some(&serde_json::Value::from(0.5_f64))
        );
    }

    /// Under `root-capacity=tuples` the family's build sizes the root from
    /// the tuple count, so a report labelled `"tuples"` timed a presized
    /// root. 100 tuples sharing one first value hold one root key: the
    /// grown root keeps 4 buckets, while the presized one has room for 100.
    #[test]
    fn hash_family_build_index_presizes_the_root_under_tuples() {
        let heap = |root_capacity| {
            let family = HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>::new(
                HashTrieConfig {
                    root_capacity,
                    ..HashTrieConfig::default()
                },
                HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
                Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
            );
            let header = RelationHeader::new("r", vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()]);
            let tuples = Tuples::from((0..100).map(|b| vec![1, b]).collect::<Vec<Vec<usize>>>());
            family
                .build_index(header, kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples))
                .heap_size_bytes()
        };
        assert!(heap(RootCapacity::Tuples) > heap(RootCapacity::Grow));
    }

    /// Under `child-capacity=tuples` the family's build sizes children from
    /// their lists, so a report labelled `"tuples"` timed sized children.
    /// Three equal tuples share one child: grown, it keeps 4 buckets; sized
    /// for its 3 tuples at 70 % it has 8. The root is presized in both arms,
    /// so only the children can differ and a `child-capacity` that resized
    /// the root instead would not pass.
    #[test]
    fn hash_family_build_index_sizes_children_under_tuples() {
        let heap = |child_capacity| {
            let family = HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>::new(
                HashTrieConfig {
                    root_capacity: RootCapacity::Tuples,
                    child_capacity,
                    ..HashTrieConfig::default()
                },
                HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
                Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
            );
            let header = RelationHeader::new("r", vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()]);
            let tuples = Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 1]; 3]);
            family
                .build_index(header, kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples))
                .heap_size_bytes()
        };
        assert!(heap(ChildCapacity::Tuples) > heap(ChildCapacity::Grow));
    }

    /// The pruning Layout reaches the relations the family builds, so a
    /// report's `ds_layout_pruning` axis describes the structure that ran.
    #[test]
    fn pruned_family_reports_the_pruning_layout() {
        let family =
            HashHtj::<kermit_iters::SipHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, EagerExpansion>::new(
                HashTrieConfig::default(),
                HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
                Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
            );
        let header = RelationHeader::new("r", vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()]);
        let tuples = Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2]]);
        let rel = family.build_index(header, kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples));
        assert_eq!(
            HashHtj::<kermit_iters::SipHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, EagerExpansion>::optimization_axes(&rel)
                .get("ds_layout_pruning"),
            Some(&serde_json::Value::String("on".into()))
        );
    }

    /// A sorted family's report axes are the relation's own.
    #[test]
    fn sorted_families_report_the_relations_seek_axis() {
        use kermit_ds::GallopingSeek;
        let family = TrieLftj::<TreeTrie<GallopingSeek>>::new(
            TreeTrieBuildMode::default(),
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
```

`count_agrees_with_join_in_every_family` becomes a test of the new pair, `count_rows` and
`execute`, which must agree in every family:

```rust
    /// `count_rows` (what `iteration` and `--verify` time and check) and the
    /// rows `execute` streams (what `kermit join` writes) come from one
    /// traversal: they must agree in every family.
    #[test]
    fn count_rows_agrees_with_execute_in_every_family() {
        fn check<F: ExecutionFamily>(family: &F) {
            // Triangles in this graph: (1, 2, 3) and (2, 3, 4).
            let edges = Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2], vec![2, 3], vec![1, 3], vec![3, 4], vec![
                2, 4,
            ]]);
            let (catalog, prepared) = prepared_over(
                RelationHeader::new_positional("edge", 2),
                edges,
                "Q(X, Y, Z) :- edge(X, Y), edge(Y, Z), edge(X, Z).",
            );
            let indexes = family.build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
            let mut streamed = Vec::new();
            family.execute(&prepared, &indexes, |row| streamed.push(row.to_vec()));
            streamed.sort();
            assert_eq!(streamed, vec![vec![1, 2, 3], vec![2, 3, 4]]);
            assert_eq!(family.count_rows(&prepared, &indexes), 2);
        }
        check(&TrieLftj::<TreeTrie>::new(
            TreeTrieBuildMode::default(),
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        ));
        check(&TrieLftj::<ColumnTrie>::new(
            ColumnTrieBuildMode::default(),
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        ));
        check(&HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>::new(
            HashTrieConfig::default(),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        ));
        check(&HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, LazyExpansion>::new(
            HashTrieConfig::default(),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        ));
    }
```

The four tests that prove a family's build mode reaches the build lose their `load`, `build_relation`
and `build_from_tuples` routes. Each now has three: the structure's `build_index`, the join
family's `build_index`, and the join family's `build_indexes`, over a query that reads `r` with its
columns swapped, so the index is a reordered one (the case the old `add_index` route covered).

```rust
    /// Both modes build identical tries, so only a spy can see whether the
    /// family's mode reached the build, on every route a relation is built.
    #[test]
    fn sorted_families_build_with_their_mode() {
        let header = || RelationHeader::new_positional("r", 2);
        let tuples = || Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2]]);
        // `r` read with its columns swapped: `build_indexes` builds a
        // reordered index.
        let (catalog, prepared) = prepared_over(header(), tuples(), "Q(X, Y) :- r(Y, X).");
        // The mode `build` hands to `build_with`, or `None` if it never does.
        let seen = |build: &dyn Fn()| {
            BUILT_WITH.take();
            build();
            BUILT_WITH.take()
        };

        for mode in [ColumnTrieBuildMode::Incremental, ColumnTrieBuildMode::Bulk] {
            let structure = SortedTrieFamily::<Spy>::new(mode);
            let join = TrieLftj::<Spy>::new(mode, Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser));
            let routes: [(&str, &dyn Fn()); 3] = [
                ("SortedTrieFamily::build_index", &|| {
                    structure.build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                }),
                ("TrieLftj::build_index", &|| {
                    join.build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                }),
                ("TrieLftj::build_indexes", &|| {
                    join.build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
                }),
            ];
            for (route, build) in routes {
                assert_eq!(seen(build), Some(mode), "{route} dropped {mode:?}");
            }
        }
    }

    /// The real `TreeTrie`, not a spy relation: its modes build identical
    /// tries, so only kermit-ds's record of parallel builds (the `test-hooks`
    /// feature) can show that the family's mode reached
    /// `TreeTrie::from_view_with_build_mode`, on every route a relation is
    /// built, reordered indexes included (#94).
    #[test]
    fn tree_trie_families_build_with_their_mode() {
        let header = || RelationHeader::new_positional("r", 2);
        let tuples = || Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2], vec![2, 1], vec![3, 4]]);
        let (catalog, prepared) = prepared_over(header(), tuples(), "Q(X, Y) :- r(Y, X).");
        // The thread count of every parallel build `build` runs.
        let parallel_builds = |build: &dyn Fn()| {
            kermit_ds::test_hooks::take_tree_trie_parallel_builds();
            build();
            kermit_ds::test_hooks::take_tree_trie_parallel_builds()
                .into_iter()
                .map(|(threads, _)| threads)
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        };

        let two = TreeTrieBuildMode::Parallel(kermit_ds::Threads::new(2).unwrap());
        for (mode, expected) in [(TreeTrieBuildMode::Serial, vec![]), (two, vec![2])] {
            let structure = SortedTrieFamily::<TreeTrie>::new(mode);
            let join = TrieLftj::<TreeTrie>::new(mode, Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser));
            let routes: [(&str, &dyn Fn()); 3] = [
                ("SortedTrieFamily::build_index", &|| {
                    structure.build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                }),
                ("TrieLftj::build_index", &|| {
                    join.build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                }),
                ("TrieLftj::build_indexes", &|| {
                    join.build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
                }),
            ];
            for (route, build) in routes {
                assert_eq!(parallel_builds(build), expected, "{route} under {mode:?}");
            }
        }
    }

    /// Both modes build tries of the same contents, so only a spy can see
    /// whether the family's mode reached the build, on every route a
    /// relation is built, eager or lazy.
    #[test]
    fn hash_families_build_with_their_mode() {
        fn check<E: ExpansionPolicy>() {
            let header = || RelationHeader::new_positional("r", 2);
            let tuples = || Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2], vec![1, 3], vec![2, 4]]);
            let (catalog, prepared) = prepared_over(header(), tuples(), "Q(X, Y) :- r(Y, X).");
            let config = HashTrieConfig::default();
            let structure = |mode| HashTrieFamily::<CountingHash, NoPruning, E>::new(config, mode);
            let join = |mode| {
                HashHtj::<CountingHash, NoPruning, E>::new(
                    config,
                    mode,
                    Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
                )
            };
            let routes: [(&str, &dyn Fn(HashTrieBuildMode)); 3] = [
                ("HashTrieFamily::build_index", &|mode| {
                    structure(mode).build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                }),
                ("HashHtj::build_index", &|mode| {
                    join(mode).build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                }),
                ("HashHtj::build_indexes", &|mode| {
                    join(mode).build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
                }),
            ];
            let hashes = |build: &dyn Fn()| {
                HASHES.set(0);
                build();
                HASHES.get()
            };
            let radix = HashTrieBuildMode::Radix(RadixBits::new(2).unwrap());
            for (route, build) in routes {
                let bulk = hashes(&|| build(HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk));
                let radixed = hashes(&|| build(radix));
                assert!(
                    radixed > bulk,
                    "{} {route}: the radix build hashed {radixed} times and the bulk build \
                     {bulk}: the mode did not reach the build",
                    E::NAME
                );
            }
        }
        check::<EagerExpansion>();
        check::<LazyExpansion>();
    }

    /// The real `HashTrie`, not the counting spy, which cannot tell

    /// the build, on every route a relation is built, reordered indexes

    #[test]
    fn hash_trie_families_build_with_their_parallel_mode() {

            let (catalog, prepared) = prepared_over(header(), tuples(), "Q(X, Y) :- r(Y, X).");
            // The record of every parallel build `build` runs.
            let parallel_builds = |build: &dyn Fn()| {

            let parallel_three = HashTrieBuildMode::Parallel(kermit_ds::Threads::new(3).unwrap());
            let presized_three = HashTrieBuildMode::Presized(kermit_ds::Threads::new(3).unwrap());

                ),
                (HashTrieConfig::default(), radix, vec![], false),
                (HashTrieConfig::default(), parallel_three, vec![3], false),
                (presized_root, HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk, vec![], false),
                (presized_root, radix, vec![], false),
                (presized_root, parallel_three, vec![3], false),
                (presized_root, presized_three, vec![3], true),
            ] {
                let structure = HashTrieFamily::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, E>::new(config, mode);
                let join = HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, E>::new(
                    config,
                    mode,
                    Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
                );
                let routes: [(&str, &dyn Fn()); 3] = [
                    ("HashTrieFamily::build_index", &|| {
                        structure.build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                    }),
                    ("HashHtj::build_index", &|| {
                        join.build_index(header(), kermit_ds::TupleView::all(&tuples()));
                    }),
                    ("HashHtj::build_indexes", &|| {
                        join.build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
                    }),
                ];
                for (route, build) in routes {
                    let builds = parallel_builds(build);
                    let threads: Vec<usize> = builds.iter().map(|b| b.threads).collect();
                    assert_eq!(
                        threads,
                        expected,
                        "{} {route} under {mode:?}, {config:?}",
                        E::NAME
                    );
                    assert!(
                        builds.iter().all(|b| b.deferred.is_some() == deferred),
                        "{} {route} under {mode:?}, {config:?}: wrong path",
                        E::NAME
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        check::<EagerExpansion>();
        check::<LazyExpansion>();
    }
```

`families_build_copies_through_build_relation` becomes a test that a reordered index carries the
family's mode and config:

```rust
    /// An index the query reads in another column order is built through
    /// `build_index` too, so it carries the family's build mode (seen by
    /// the spy) and config (seen on the index).
    #[test]
    fn families_build_reordered_indexes_with_their_mode_and_config() {
        let header = || RelationHeader::new_positional("edge", 2);
        let edges = || Tuples::from(vec![vec![1, 2], vec![1, 3], vec![2, 3]]);
        // `edge` read with its columns swapped: the one index is columns [1, 0].
        let (catalog, prepared) = prepared_over(header(), edges(), "Q(X, Y) :- edge(Y, X).");

        let join = TrieLftj::<Spy>::new(
            ColumnTrieBuildMode::Incremental,
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        );
        BUILT_WITH.take();
        let indexes = join.build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
        assert_eq!(BUILT_WITH.take(), Some(ColumnTrieBuildMode::Incremental));
        let columns: Vec<&[usize]> = indexes
            .iter()
            .map(|(spec, _)| spec.columns.as_slice())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(columns, vec![&[1, 0][..]]);
        let (_, index) = indexes.iter().next().expect("one index");
        assert_eq!(index.header().name(), "edge");
        assert_eq!(index.header().arity(), 2);

        let config = HashTrieConfig {
            load_factor: LoadFactor::percent(50).unwrap(),
            ..HashTrieConfig::default()
        };
        let hash = HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>::new(
            config,
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        );
        let indexes = hash.build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
        let (_, index) = indexes.iter().next().expect("one index");
        assert_eq!(index.config(), &config);
        assert_eq!(index.header().name(), "edge");
    }
```

`build_index_of_an_empty_source_accepts_any_header`,
`build_indexes_builds_each_index_by_the_familys_mode_and_config`,

- `assert_view_builds_like_batch` (doc starts `` /// `build_index` over `view` builds the relation that `build_relation` ``) compared the view's build with `build_relation`. It now compares it with the build of the view's materialisation:

```rust
    /// `build_index` over `view` builds the relation that `build_index`
    /// builds over the identity view of the view's materialisation: the same
    /// tuples, the same count and the same heap.
    fn assert_view_builds_like_batch<F: RelationFamily>(family: &F, view: &TupleView<'_>) {
        let header = || RelationHeader::new_positional("r", view.arity());
        let materialised = view.materialize();
        let from_view = family.build_index(header(), view.clone());
        let from_batch = family.build_index(header(), TupleView::all(&materialised));
        let (mut viewed, mut batched) = (visited::<F>(&from_view), visited::<F>(&from_batch));
        viewed.sort();
        batched.sort();
        assert_eq!(viewed, batched);
        assert_eq!(F::tuple_count(&from_view), F::tuple_count(&from_batch));
        assert_eq!(from_view.heap_size_bytes(), from_batch.heap_size_bytes());
    }
```

- `prepared_over_r` (the helper above `build_indexes_builds_each_index_by_the_familys_mode_and_config`, doc starts ``/// A catalog holding the relation `r` ``) builds its own `Planner`. - `assert_pipelines_agree` and `execute_and_count_rows_agree_with_the_old_engine_in_every_family` (the helper from its doc comment `` /// Runs `text` over `edges` through `family`'s old engine and through its `` and the test from its doc comment `` /// `execute` and `count_rows` answer what the old engine answers, in `` ) compared the new pipeline with the old engine. Replace both, together, with a check of the new pipeline against the hand-counted answers they already carry:

```rust
    /// Runs `text` over `edges` through `family`'s per-query pipeline: the
    /// rows `execute` streams number the hand-counted `expected`, and
    /// `count_rows` counts the same.
    fn assert_pipeline_answers<F: ExecutionFamily>(
        family: &F, edges: &Tuples, text: &str, expected: u64,
    ) {
        let (catalog, prepared) =
            prepared_over(RelationHeader::new_positional("edge", 2), edges.clone(), text);
        let indexes = family.build_indexes(&catalog, &prepared);
        let mut rows = Vec::new();
        family.execute(&prepared, &indexes, |row| rows.push(row.to_vec()));
        assert_eq!(rows.len() as u64, expected, "{text}");
        assert_eq!(family.count_rows(&prepared, &indexes), expected, "{text}");
    }

    /// `execute` and `count_rows` answer the hand-counted rows in every
    /// family: a self-join, a constant, a repeated variable, a placeholder
    /// and a query whose index reads `edge` reversed.
    #[test]
    fn execute_and_count_rows_answer_in_every_family() {
        // The edges 1 to 2, 2 to 3, 1 to 3, 3 to 4, 2 to 4, and the loop on 4.
        let mut edges = Tuples::new(2);
        for (src, dst) in [(1, 2), (2, 3), (1, 3), (3, 4), (2, 4), (4, 4)] {
            edges.push(&[src, dst]);
        }
        let queries = [
            // Triangles: (1,2,3), (2,3,4), (2,4,4), (3,4,4) and (4,4,4).
            ("Q(X, Y, Z) :- edge(X, Y), edge(Y, Z), edge(X, Z).", 5),
            // A constant: the successors of 1.
            ("Q(Y) :- edge(c1, Y).", 2),
            // A repeated variable: the loop.
            ("Q(X) :- edge(X, X).", 1),
            // A placeholder: one row per edge.
            ("Q(X) :- edge(X, _).", 6),
            // The index reads `edge` reversed.
            ("Q(Y, X) :- edge(X, Y).", 6),
        ];

        let tree = TrieLftj::<TreeTrie>::new(
            TreeTrieBuildMode::default(),
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        );
        let column = TrieLftj::<ColumnTrie>::new(
            ColumnTrieBuildMode::default(),
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        );
        let hash = HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, NoPruning, EagerExpansion>::new(
            HashTrieConfig::default(),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        );
        let lazy = HashHtj::<SipHashStrategy, SingletonPruning, LazyExpansion>::new(
            HashTrieConfig::default(),
            HashTrieBuildMode::Bulk,
            Planner::stored(LexicographicOptimiser),
        );
        for (text, expected) in queries {
            assert_pipeline_answers(&tree, &edges, text, expected);
            assert_pipeline_answers(&column, &edges, text, expected);
            assert_pipeline_answers(&hash, &edges, text, expected);
            assert_pipeline_answers(&lazy, &edges, text, expected);
        }
    }
```

## Story 20: The old `kermit::db` pipeline goes

- **Developer:** intermediate-dev
- **Files:** `kermit/src/db.rs`, `kermit/src/db/database.rs`, `kermit/src/db/validation.rs`, `kermit/src/db/lifecycle.rs`, `kermit/src/lib.rs`, `kermit/src/bench/workload.rs`, `kermit-ds/src/tuple_scan.rs`, `kermit/tests/translator_round_trip.rs`, `kermit/tests/job_translate.rs`, `kermit/tests/cli_query_errors.rs`, `kermit-generate/src/snap.rs`, `kermit-generate/src/sink.rs`
- **Interfaces:** exposes the final `lftj_join*`, `hash_join*` and `validate_query` (Names contract: kermit::db) to Stories 22–23; uses Stories 9, 12 and 19
- **Verify:** `cargo test -p kermit --lib db`
- **Review:** deep (`compute_join` is a landmine marker; this story rebuilds it)

Deletes what the new lifecycle replaced and moves the library surface onto it. `Database<R>`, `JoinFamily` with `SortedFamily` and `HashFamily`, the copy protocol (`required_indexes`, `add_index`, `clear_indexes`, `build_index`, `index_header`) and the private `Planned`, `plan_query` and `run_join` go, with `kermit/src/db/database.rs` and the old validation rewrites. The four entry points keep their names, and still share one private body, but take a `&Catalog` and run `prepare`, `build` and `execute`; the hash entry point loses its `H`, which existed only to hash constants. `validate_query(query, relations)` loses the column-order policy and with it the cyclic and reserved-name checks; it keeps today's check order and decides constants through `extract_accesses`, so `JoinError` drops `ReservedRelationName`, `CyclicAttributeOrder` and `MissingIndex` and keeps every other variant and message; `Workload::prepare` (Story 17) loses its third argument to `validate_query` too. `compute_join`, which used to call `JoinAlgo::join_iter` past validation, now builds a `Catalog` and runs the same three steps. Its code holds the landmine marker `compute_join`, so **the supervisor should dispatch this story's developer with `effort: xhigh`**. Two tasks, each leaving the tree green: Task 20.1 rebuilds `compute_join` over the lifecycle Story 12 added, and Task 20.2 makes the single coupled switch of the entry points, `validate_query`, `JoinError`, the callers of `validate_query` (`Workload::prepare` and two test files), the CLI test for the reserved name, the doc of `TupleScan` in `kermit-ds/src/tuple_scan.rs`, which names the `Database` that goes, and two docs in `kermit-generate` (`snap.rs` and `sink.rs`) that cite the dropped `CyclicAttributeOrder` error and the reserved prefixes as reasons (the code switch and the reserved-name test cannot be split: the old pipeline constructs the dropped error variants, and the CLI test would fail the moment validation stops reserving the prefixes). `Planner::new` takes a column-order policy until Story 23 retires it, and `prepare` plans freely under any planner, so the two places that build one here (`compute_join`, inline, and one helper in the tests of `db`) pass `ColumnOrderPolicy::Any`; Story 23 changes those two lines. Task 20.2 starts by checking that Stories 14 to 19 left no user of the old API outside `kermit/src/db*`.

```rust
/// Convenience function that builds relations from raw tuple batches and runs a
/// join, returning the result tuples.
///
/// Constructs a synthetic Datalog query from the `variables` and
/// `rel_variables` mappings (variable `v` is written `V{v}`, and input `i` is
/// the relation `R{i}`), loads the batches into a [`db::Catalog`], and runs
/// the same [`db::prepare`], [`db::build`] and [`db::execute`] steps as
/// [`db::lftj_join`] and [`db::hash_join`], with `R` as the index structure
/// and `JA` as the algorithm. The query is therefore validated first, a
/// variable repeated within one `rel_variables` entry selects the rows whose
/// columns agree, and each result row holds the `variables`, in that order:
/// a variable only the body binds is not part of it.
///
/// An empty batch carries no arity (an empty `Vec` converts to arity 0), so
/// a relation with no rows takes its arity from its atom. An empty
/// `rel_variables` entry stands for the unary atom `R{i}(_)`.
///
/// # Panics
///
/// If the synthetic query cannot run over the inputs: a head variable no
/// relation binds, a repeated head variable, or a batch whose arity is not
/// the length of its `rel_variables` entry. The message is the
/// [`db::JoinError`]'s.
pub fn compute_join<R, JA>(
    input: Vec<impl Into<Tuples>>, variables: Vec<usize>, rel_variables: Vec<Vec<usize>>,
) -> Vec<Vec<usize>>
where
    R: Relation,
    JA: JoinAlgo<R>,
{
    // Build a synthetic query from the legacy inputs
    // Head: Q(V0, V1, ...)
    let head_vars: Vec<String> = variables.iter().map(|v| format!("V{}", v)).collect();
    // Body: R{i}(V...)
    let mut body_preds: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (i, rv) in rel_variables.iter().enumerate() {
        let var_list = if rv.is_empty() {
            "_".to_string()
        } else {
            rv.iter()
                .map(|v| format!("V{}", v))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        };
        body_preds.push(format!("R{}({})", i, var_list));
    }
    let query_str = format!("Q({}) :- {}.", head_vars.join(", "), body_preds.join(", "));
    let query: JoinQuery = query_str.parse().expect("Failed to build JoinQuery");

    // One catalog relation per batch, named as the query's atoms name them.
    // A batch with no rows carries no arity (an empty `Vec` converts to arity
    // 0), so it takes its atom's: one column per term, or one for `_`.
    let relations: Vec<(RelationHeader, Tuples)> = input
        .into_iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, tuples)| {
            let tuples: Tuples = tuples.into();
            let tuples = match rel_variables.get(i) {
                | Some(terms) if tuples.is_empty() => Tuples::new(terms.len().max(1)),
                | _ => tuples,
            };
            (
                RelationHeader::new_positional(format!("R{i}"), tuples.arity()),
                tuples,
            )
        })
        .collect();

    // Synthetic queries carry no constants and this helper predates
    // statistics, so plan with the stats-free default optimiser.
    // `Planner::new` still takes a policy; `prepare` plans freely under any.
    let planner = Planner::new(Box::new(LexicographicOptimiser), ColumnOrderPolicy::Any);
    let catalog = Catalog::new(relations, planner.required_statistics());
    let prepared = prepare(&catalog, &query, &planner)
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("compute_join: {error}"));
    let indexes = build::<R>(&catalog, &prepared);
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    execute::<R, JA>(&prepared, &indexes, |row| rows.push(row.to_vec()));
    rows
}
```
